json.name: vllm
json.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs

json.name: v0.34.0
json.body:
# v0.34.0 **1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new).** Thank you! ## TL;DR - **10 new models** (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!) - **Extensible KV cache is on by default:** vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now **remove `gpu_memory_utilization`** from your configs. - **Model Runner V1 is gone.** Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner. - **Big speedups** on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3). - **Upgrade check:** default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0` is required. See [Before you upgrade](#before-you-upgrade). ## Before you upgrade > [!IMPORTANT] > These changes can break existing setups. | Change | What to do | PR | |---|---|---| | Model Runner V1 removed | Remove `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`; it now fails at startup. Port V1 logits processors to `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor`. | #63373 | | Default `--block-size` is 64 (was 16) | Pass `--block-size 16` to keep the old behavior. ROCm paged attention still uses 16. | #63231 | | Extensible KV cache on by default; `gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0 | **In most cases it's now best to not set `gpu_memory_utilization`**. This should provide maximum kv cache capacity while avoiding runtime OOMs. Use it to share a GPU with other processes or when extensible kv cache is disabled. | #56492 | | ROCm 7.2 artifacts dropped | Use the ROCm 10.0 wheels and images. `-rocm72` is no longer published. | #61939 | | `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0` required | Also requires `tokenizers >= 0.23.3` and `timm >= 1.0.30`. | #64779 | | QuTLASS / `fp_quant` removed | `fp_quant` checkpoints no longer load. | #65230 | | Marlin W4A8 removed | Use `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` instead of `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE`. | #65542 | | Keye-VL and Keye-VL-1.5 removed | — | #64287 | All breaking changes, deprecations and new defaults are listed in [the full changelog](#full-changelog). ## New models | Model | Notes | PR | |---|---|---| | **Mistral Large 4** | 1T total / 52B active, FP8 and NVFP4. Runs on NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350. | #64534 | | MiniMax-M3.1-Flash | Blackwell NVFP4 and ROCm kernels, DSpark draft | #64111 | | NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe | 30B-A4B speech model: audio chat and `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | #64282 | | Ricursive Ripple-65B Preview | BF16 and NVFP4, `ripple` reasoning and tool parsers | #65745 | | Zyphra ZAYA1 | ZAYA1-8B, ZAYA1-74B-preview | #65302 | | Baidu Unlimited-OCR-2 | DASH sparse attention | #64016 | | Liquid AI LFM3, LFM3-VL, LFM3-Audio | | #65826, #65827, #65828 | | NVIDIA Canary-1B-v2 | ASR and X↔En translation | #64215 | | Ming3-ASR | | #63585 | | NVIDIA Parakeet TDT | Through the vllm-parakeet-plugin | #65005 | ## Highlights ### Extensible KV cache, on by default - On CUDA and ROCm, the KV cache is sized from memory actually free **after** CUDA graph capture and warmup, not from an estimate (#56492). - **Result:** a larger cache (e.g. MiniMax-M3 on H200: 433k → 672k tokens), so throughput is higher and TTFT lower at high concurrency. - **Trade-off:** per-token decode latency can rise on some models (TPOT +6–18% on some H200 models at concurrency 128). Opt out with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` or `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`. - Hardened with fixes for allocator fragmentation, startup OOMs and KV connectors (#67296, #67485, #66731, #66523, #66197, #65137, #66605, #66674). ### Model Runner V2 only - Model Runner V1 is removed (#63373). - Dual-batch overlap now runs on MRV2, including with speculative decoding and DCP (#61464). ### Speculative decoding - **Suffix decoding** runs on MRV2 with a GPU speculator; Arctic Inference is no longer needed (#60339). - **Custom speculators:** declarative configs plus a `register_speculative_method` plugin API (#63205). - **CUDA graphs** for MRV2 draft-model speculators (#60989). - **Adaptive verification** works with XPress (#65175). - **Draft KV cache matches the target's dtype**, so an FP8 target gets an FP8 draft cache (#65198). ### Performance | Improvement | Hardware | Gain | PR | |---|---|---|---| | Step5 NVFP4 MoE on TRTLLM-Gen | 4×GB200 | up to **1.95×** decode | #65152 | | GLM-5.3-Flash DeepGEMM FP8 MegaMoE | NVIDIA | **1.6×** output throughput vs DEP4 | #60895 | | Muse Spark Open specialized decode (opt-in) | GB300 | **1.5×** single-stream decode | #64077 | | Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill under TP (default) | GB200 | GLM-5.3 TTFT **1.24–1.40×** faster at 32K–128K | #63956 | | KV-balanced MLA decode for Kimi-K3 (opt-in) | GB300 | **1.34–1.59×** decode attention | #63638 | | Qwen3.5 on breakable CUDA graphs (no torch.compile) | NVIDIA | **3.0–8.8%** lower decode ITL | #51012 | | FlyDSL decode monokernel, Muse Spark Open DSpark | 8×MI355X | **+35–57%** interactivity at conc. 1–8 | #63440 | ### AMD ROCm - Release images and wheels are **ROCm 10.0 only** (#61939). - MoRI EPv2 via `--all2all-backend mori` (#61361). - Kimi-K3 specialized decode on MI355X, opt-in (#61435). - TRITON_ATTN is the default attention backend on RDNA3 and RDNA4 (#60418). ### Serving and operations - **Checkpoint/restore** (CRIU + `cuda-checkpoint`) through `/checkpoint/prepare`, `/checkpoint/status` and `/checkpoint/restore`, in both the Python and Rust frontends (#62570). - **Fault-tolerant DP+EP scale-down:** dead ranks are removed and their experts redistributed without a restart (#46370). - Best-effort **NUMA binding** on by default (#61258). - Opt-in **cache-aware admission** ordering (#54625). - Rust frontend: stateless **Responses API** (#63902) and **`n > 1`** (#65625). ## Install **Python wheels** | Platform | Install | |---|---| | CUDA 13.0 (PyPI) | `pip install vllm` | | CUDA 13.0 (uv) | `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto` | | ROCm 10.0 | `pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/0.34.0/rocm100` | | XPU | `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.34.0/xpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu --index-strategy unsafe-best-match` | **Docker images** | Platform | Image | Short alias | |---|---|---| | CUDA 13.0 (default) | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.34.0` | `vllm/vllm:v0.34.0` | | CUDA 13.0 + DeepEP over AWS EFA | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.34.0-efa` | `vllm/vllm:v0.34.0-efa` | | ROCm 10.0 | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.34.0` | `vllm/vllm:v0.34.0-rocm` | | CPU | `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.34.0` | `vllm/vllm:v0.34.0-cpu` | | XPU | `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.34.0` | `vllm/vllm:v0.34.0-xpu` | `latest` tags work the same way (e.g. `vllm/vllm:latest-rocm`). The default CUDA image now includes the AWS EFA userspace (libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl). The `-efa` image adds DeepEP built for EFA and routes NCCL over EFA by default (#65576). The **Assets** section below has the source tarball and the CUDA 13.0 (x86_64, arm64), CPU (x86_64, arm64, macOS) and XPU (x86_64) wheels. ## Full changelog
Model support - **Mistral Large 4** (#64534) runs on MRV2 with: - sparse MLA plus the DSA indexer, and cross-layer KV sharing; - DSpark, DCP/PCP, NIXL P/D and HiSparse. - **Other new models:** - MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (#64111), plus P/D across different prefill and decode TP (#64475). - Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe with MTP and DFlash2 (#64282, #64944). - **DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1** - Prefill gathers compressed KV once per KV-source group: 38 → 4 gathers per step (#59131). - Decoder replay graphs share the model graph pool: prefill graph memory 15.52 → 9.88 GiB per rank on GB200 (#63155). - `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` 3.5× faster, prefill 6% faster (#63540). - DSpark/MTP memory savings of about 512 MiB per GPU (#63996). - Engram host tables shared across DP ranks (#62359). - DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits on the FP8 indexer cache (#62011). - Packed multi-image vision encoding, 1.6–2.6× (#65030). - LoRA on the language model, compressor and `wo_a` layers (#57245, #64880). - DSpark with PCP (#61994); PCP with PP or DP (#63098). - Fixes: sparse prefill in FULL CUDA graphs (#59986), prefill memory budgeting (#63047), MTP embedding under PP (#65816), DeepSeek-V3.2 PP (#59961). - **GLM** - GLM-5.3-Flash: DeepGEMM FP8 MegaMoE (#60895), adaptive verification (#60229), row-strided QKV into FlashKDA (#61614). - GLM-5.3 FP8 MoE sorted-A TMA on H200, 6.0–7.6% E2E throughput (#64760). - FP8 KV cache for DSpark and DFlash drafts (#63841, #64612, #65553). - FP32 indexer MQA logits restored for GLM-5/GLM-5.3/HY-V4, with new `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` (#64580). - Fused KDA convs fix stale weights after RL refit (#60991). - **Muse Spark** - Opt-in Muse Spark Open specialized decode on GB300 (#64077). - One RoPE cache shared across layers: 11.5 GiB per GPU saved, 14.5% more KV cache on 8×B200 (#65206). - GEMM and communication+norm fusions (#65438, #64638); hybrid DeepGEMM MegaMoE / TRT-LLM for NVFP4 (#64525). - CUDA routing kernel (#64553), MegaMoE JIT warmup (#63920), DSpark draft loading fix (#65125). - **MiniMax-M3 / M3.1** - Sequence parallelism and GEMM-RS for TP + MegaMoE, 14–20% lower P50 TTFT (#64659), also with PP (#65537). - Fused norm + MXFP8 quant, 1.39–1.60× (#64852). - Triton query-tiled sparse prefill on Hopper (#57420); SM90 split-K indexer (#64037). - No host sync in prefill metadata (#65883); NVFP4 MegaMoE warmup (#66227); fmha_sm100 indexer updates (#66228). - Fixes: M3.1 prefill workspace (#64856), sequence parallelism (#65496), encoder CUDA graphs (#65226). - **Kimi** - Opt-in `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` for agentic workloads on Blackwell (#63638). - Kimi-K3 MegaMoE symmetric buffer 10.73 → 2.50 GiB per GPU at TP8 EP (#63541). - FlashInfer fused FP8 chunked-context K/V pack (#61527). - Fixes: KDA prefill OOM (#63989), NaNs via FlashKDA/FlashMLA pins (#64759), sleep mode (#64583, #66273). - Kimi K3.1 groundwork landed (#66030, #66028), but **K3.1 is not servable in this release**. - **Qwen** - Qwen3.5: breakable CUDA graphs instead of torch.compile (#51012); fused norm/gate + quant (#64509) and AR + norm + quant (#64723); GDN `in_proj` overlap (#64425, #64999). - GDN prefill state gather/scatter fused for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 and Kimi KDA, 1.16–1.50× (#66064). - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: PLE disk offload via `--engram-config '{"disk_offload": true}'` (27 GiB less on DGX Spark, #59958), PP (#60234), shared QSA top-k buffer (#65619), loading fixes (#62318, #65812, #64820, #60490). - Fixes: long-context int32 overflow (#63761), multi-layer MTP (#62111). - **Other models** - Step5 MegaMoE with PP (#65504) and KV block sizing (#65153). - Gemma 4: multimodal encoder DP (#60314), PP (#65989), FA4 FP8 MMA on SM90 (#60372). - Moved to the Transformers modeling backend: OLMoE (#63384), Gemma v1 and StableLM (#66393), Aria (#59767; temporarily about 11% less KV cache and 25% lower image throughput). - Matryoshka dimensions for EmbeddingGemma 2 (#64885, #60978); RADIO C-RADIO v2/v3/v4 (#58468). - Qwen3-ASR on the upstream Transformers config; no `--hf-overrides` needed for the ForceAligner (#66097, #63274). - Fixes: GPT-OSS MXFP4 LoRA (#65825), PLaMo3 GPTQ (#62836), Ling3 (#65088), DomynEdge (#66819). - **Multimodal** - Encoder CUDA graphs for Pixtral/Mistral3 (#56277), shared capture buffers (#65084), one replay per batch up to `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (#65227). - On-device input normalization for Nemotron VL (#57924), Gemma 3 (#64487), Gemma 4 (#65577). - `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data` for MiMo-V2.6 (#64179). - Fixes: FlashInfer ViT attention on GLM-4.1V/GLM-OCR/GLM-5.3-Flash (#65778), Qwen3-Omni and Qwen2.5-Omni video budgets (#66017, #66190), dots_ocr with TP (#64543), embedding-only startup (#65689), media cache eviction (#65363).
Engine core - **Extensible KV cache** - On by default on CUDA and ROCm (#56492). - Headroom for measured allocator fragmentation, validated on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 at TP8+EP on 8×H200 (#67296). - Fixes: sizing and startup OOMs (#67485, #66523, #66731, #66197, #65554), connectors that failed to start (#65225), up to 84% undersized caches on DGX Spark (#65413), `--max-model-len auto` (#65463). - Startup warning when an explicit `gpu_memory_utilization` withholds memory from it (#66704); docs on when to set it (#67071). - **Model Runner V2** - The only runner after MRV1's removal (#63373); DBO with spec decode and DCP (#61464). - Separate prefill (token) and decode (request) CUDA graph capture sizes (#63406). - Staged writes copied straight into UVA (#63633); idle sampler writes skipped, about 10–11% faster small-batch decode (#62748). - Sampler warmed up after graph capture to stop memory growth under load (#62560). - Lower peak memory for chunked prompt logprobs (#64841, #64914); Triton ReplaySSM (#65033). - NVIDIA Confidential Computing decode fixes (#59981). - **Speculative decoding** - Suffix decoding (#60339) and custom speculators (#63205) on MRV2; draft-model CUDA graphs (#60989). - XPress with adaptive verification (#65175); adaptive verification draft budgets on a Triton kernel (#63421). - Batch-sharded draft logits (#63554); DSpark sequential blocks (#63886). - DSpark sliding-window MLA draft layers (#63795) under DCP (#63796); fused Markov sampling, 42–50% less sampling time (#64476); `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#64368). - Draft KV cache dtype aligned with the target (#65198). - Trace replay with ngram/EAGLE3/MTP, 1.47–2.03× (#63275); 3× faster resample kernel (#65100). - Fixes: DFlash acceptance of 0 with FULL CUDA graphs (#64059), a resample race (#66048), acceptance-estimator cancellation (#65229), standalone draft prefill under FULL graphs (#65804), grammar-invalid drafts (#61557). - **Scheduler and engine overhead** - Prompt token ids kept as int32 buffers: 40× less per-request CPU on a 128K prompt (#62702). - Per-request id lists kept out of the cyclic GC (#65300); 45–50% less KV block allocation CPU (#65831). - New requests and aborts handled while waiting for model output (#65466), with a cheaper wait loop (#65773). - Opt-in cache-aware admission via `--cache-aware-admission-window` (#54625). - `--max-num-inflight-kv-loads` starts async KV loads while the batch is full (#65319), with cached reservations: 47.2 → 5.4 ms per schedule (#65285). - A multimodal item is no longer split by a prefix hit (#65271). - **Startup and compile** - No openai/fastapi imports in EngineCore and workers (#65423, #65589). - CUDA graph memory profile skipped when its estimate is disabled (#64622). - Device-neutral compile cache via `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK`, on by default (#63247); all graph-affecting config fields hashed into compile cache keys (#65652). - `--shuffle-safetensors-files` for large EP startups (#42837). - `BasevLLMParameter`'s Python `__torch_function__` dropped: GLM-5.2-FP8 TTFT −6.1% on GB300 (#63785). - **Lifecycle** - Process checkpoint/restore over HTTP (#62570); opt-in multi-worker CUDA checkpoint sleep (#64186). - Best-effort NUMA binding by default; `--no-numa-bind` to disable (#61258). - Sleep mode with exact-size pinned backups, up to about 578 GiB less host memory per node on Mistral Large 4 TP8 (#64630); level 2 discards only parameters (#66010, #66165, #59994). - Fast Start weight-cache restarts for online FP8/MXFP8, ModelOpt CUTLASS FP8/NVFP4/block-FP8 and AWQ/GPTQ Marlin (#63672, #63754, #64119, #64182), with pluggable shared warmup-cache stores (#65168). - `WatermarkConfig.enforce` (#62966). - **RL and weight loading** - `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` writes checkpoint tensors straight into the live model (#64336, #64352, #65281). - Every load and update finishes through `finalize_model_weights` (#65914, #64357, #64692, #57678). - Load plans for weight-transfer engines (#65235); per-update NCCL source ranks for PP trainers (#62557). - Sparse weight patches validated in one pass, 40–48% shorter pause (#66021). - Offloaded KV tier survives pause/sleep (#57810); partial stacked weights rejected (#63752). - **LoRA** - MoE-LoRA shrink/expand kernels up to 64 tokens (#64653); embedding LoRA scaled by `embed_scale` (#62470). - Rejected: adapters on unwrapped modules (#63489), non-linear expert placement with EP (#62797). - Fixes: reloads with requests in flight (#64616), KV-sharing fast prefill (#61162), SEQ_CLS heads (#63286), fused MoE expand rounding (#63894), Mamba-1 (#64681). - **Batch invariance:** LFM2 ShortConv (#62367), FlashInfer FP8 bmm and W4A16 NVFP4 (#62192), GPTQ (#60479), FA sliding window (#65627), `aten::mm` out_dtype overloads (#60047).
Large-scale serving - **Expert parallelism and fault tolerance** - DP+EP scale-down via `POST /v1/fault_tolerance/apply` (#46370); MoRI EPv2 (#61361). - Opt-in `symm_mem` EPLB weight-migration backend (#62009). - `--enable-ep-weight-filter` with EPLB: DeepSeek-R1 NVFP4 DEP8 reads 105 GiB per rank instead of 385 GiB (#64187). - `num_redundant_experts` defaults to the minimum valid value (#30614). - Skipped combine staging copy in `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` (#65498); DeepEP V2 padded rows (#54109). - **Context parallelism and sparse attention** - Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill under TP (#63956); DCP on the FlashMLA sparse bf16 KV path (#61609). - MLA decode up-projected before the A2A merge with `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` (#64994); faster DCP sparse-indexer top-k (#65178, #64129). - Cross-layer KV cache sharing for MLA layers (#64095). - Fixes: PP rank derivation under PCP (#65539), FlashInfer MLA DCP decode (#59392). - **KV connectors** - NIXL: push mode via `transfer_mode` (#64230); `ucx_backend_params` (rocm_ipc on MI355X: 3.4 → 483.7 Gbps, #62905); 38% fewer hybrid SSM transfer bytes (#62317); block pairing across different P/D block sizes (#59746), with mismatched push handshakes rejected (#59747); same-host NVLink with the extensible KV cache (#65137). - Mooncake: selective leases (#63420), automatic `cache_prefix` (#65160), per-GPU RDMA devices (#65076), heterogeneous-TP hybrid sharing (#54307), sleep mode (#59934), lease renewal (#64193). - Lookahead block hashes in NIXL, Mooncake and offloading connectors (#64096); UMBP standalone mode (#61795, #61793). - Out-of-tree and LMCache MP connectors with the extensible KV cache (#66605, #66674). - **KV offload** - SimpleCPUOffload with one host buffer per rank and opt-in HugeTLB pages (#60130); no zero-filled pool (#64345). - KVCR v0.2.0 (#64224, #63889); async lookups published per request group (#57474); secondary tiers rejected on multi-node engines (#62930). - Hardened P2P tier (#63781, #64250, #64256, #64251, #64501, #63618, #64300, #63988) and correctness fixes (#64229, #63566, #65279, #65631, #64400, #63937, #65640). - **HiSparse** - Uses the extensible KV cache by default: 16% more GPU+host KV capacity (#65214). - Fused slot invalidation, up to 1.8% lower TPOT on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 (#60103); fewer hash probes (#61263); speculative-group prefetch (#63801). - Platform backend for hardware plugins (#62592); scheduler deadlock fix (#62979). - **EPD and distributed** - Metadata-only image and video inputs for GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4.1 (#64071, #62802). - Bitwise-identical 1-stage and 2-stage custom all-reduce (#57042); FlashInfer all-reduce gated on 16-byte rows (#63123). - Cross-node MNNVL groups kept off CUDA IPC all-reduce (#55835).
Hardware - **NVIDIA** - Step5 NVFP4 TRTLLM-Gen MoE (#65152). - DeepSeek-V4.1: latency_specialized decode extended, 5.9–17% faster decode step on GB300 (#63921); swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention for TP2/TP4, 1.4–2.15× (#62633); opt-in fused DSpark Markov sampling, 1.6–3.9× (#64442). - Sparse-indexer top-k reads BF16 logits directly (#62172, #64138); single-launch fused prefill top-k (#60618). - GLM-5.3 TMA MoE projections on H200 and SM100 (#63820, #65746); SM90 native small-head sparse FlashMLA, +10% on GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 (#64510). - CuTe DSL BF16x3 router GEMM for fp32 routers on Hopper (#61903); fused GDN MTP decode for DSpark K=8, +18% on B300 (#65874). - GLM-5.3-Flash on 2× DGX Spark, 15% lower TPOT (#62956); faster weight loading on integrated GPUs (#58868). - Rubin locality-domain NVFP4 MoE (#61685); Jetson Thor (SM110) fixes (#62133, #65050, #62275). - **AMD ROCm** - ROCm 10.0 only (#61939); AITER v0.1.28.post1 (#63774, #65937); MoRI EPv2 (#61361). - MonoKernel decode for Muse Spark Open DSpark verify (#63440), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP8 (#64101) and the MiniMax-M3.1 DSpark drafter, +10% P90 interactivity (#65386). - Kimi-K3 specialized decode (#61435), AITER-tuned prefill GEMMs: mean TTFT 5.35 → 4.05 s (#63730), opt-in FlyDSL FP8 MLA prefill (#59124). - DeepSeek-V4-Pro P/D over MoRIIO (#48989); Step-5-Preview (#61837) and Reflection Beam 1.0 (#62057) on ROCm. - RDNA: TRITON_ATTN by default (#60418), AITER Triton kernels on RDNA3 (#52970), HIP GDN prefill backend for gfx1151 (#56307), opt-in W4A16 dense prefill cache: TTFT −22 to −26% on Strix Halo (#60710). - Fixes: Kimi-K2.6 int4 prefill regression on Triton 3.8 (#62565), MI355 extensible KV cache OOMs (#65418). - **Intel XPU** - PyTorch 2.15 (#63977) and vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.17 with new MoE/MLA interfaces (#60609). - Per-token dynamic FP8 activations (#61362); faster batched Triton MoE (#51605); MRoPE kernel (#59938); GDN metadata reuse (#64479); DeepSeek-V4 adaptive verification (#62309). - **CPU** - MRV2 on CPU backends without Triton: Arm, IBM Z, PowerPC, RISC-V (#61995). - zentorch 2.14.0.2 (#65669) and Laguna MoE on Zen (#63711). - Faster GDN spec-decode updates (#64829); Gemma 4 MoE gelu_tanh (#61593); bidirectional encoder-only attention (#63738). - **Other:** out-of-tree layer overrides via `vllm.model_executor.hw_agnostic.resolve` (#60218); shared routed-expert row restorers (#64689); Ascend Triton fix (#64013).
Quantization - New `--quantization lut_b_moe`: about 3.14-bit MoE experts with MXFP8 activations, native on Rubin (#62759). - `w4afp8` checkpoints on the W4A8 FP8 MoE path (#64410). - Block Hadamard input rotation with online `mxfp4_hadamard32` and Quark online-rotation checkpoints (#62750). - CSF-compressed NVFP4 block scales in ModelOpt (#64312); activation quant overrides for online MXFP4 (#51808). - DeepSeek-V4.1 MXFP8 linears on cuBLASLt (#64815); 3× faster MXFP4 activation quant (#63101); faster FP8 quant on SM100+ (#61641). - QuIP NVFP4 on Humming (#65230). - Fixes: NVFP4 NaN logits (#63382, #61755), Humming FP8 (#60163, #56606), hadacore (#63514).
API and frontend - **New endpoints and options** - `/checkpoint/prepare`, `/checkpoint/status`, `/checkpoint/restore` (#62570). - `thinking_token_budget` on `/v1/responses` (#63896); `/v1/completions` in `vllm run-batch` (#64097). - Streaming derender on `/inference/v1/generate` (#63103). - Anthropic Messages API: `min_tokens` (#65459) and `thinking.type=between_tools` (#65954). - `vllm:request_render_duration_seconds` histogram (#60213). - **Tool calling and reasoning** - New `granite_toolcall_parser` for Granite 4.2 (#65216); llama3_json moved to the ParserEngine (#63569). - Incremental streaming for Kimi K3 (#62203), `tool_choice="required"` (#60882), DeepSeek V4/V3.2 (#58780), GLM-4.7 (#64535), Qwen3 (#64675). - Fixes: DeepSeek V4.1 (#62517, #64971, #62729, #62647), GLM-4.7 (#64615), Step3 (#65274), FunctionGemma (#63992), union/enum string parameters (#64518). - **Behavior** - Corrupt or oversized images and disabled local media return 400 instead of 500 (#63433, #60308, #64032). - Responses accepts incomplete assistant/reasoning history, e.g. from Codex (#35508). - Multi-template processors use the default template (#63606); an empty `tools` array is accepted like OpenAI (#65547). - The first streamed usage reports cached prompt tokens (#65036); plain completion stream frames render about 9× faster (#52875). - **Rust frontend** - Stateless Responses API (#63902) with namespace tools (#65853); `n > 1` (#65625); `--skip-tokenizer-init` (#64697). - Hybrid and external DP load balancing (#64451, #64450); native GLM-5.3 chat rendering (#62424). - Prompt block hashing off the engine's GIL (#63842); `--reasoning-effort-map` (#62312). - `--enable-log-outputs`, `--max-log-len`, `--root-path`, `--log-error-stack` (#63769, #64223, #64222, #65001). - More request, response and metric parity with Python (#65293, #65294, #65623, #65624, #64218, #64526, #63964, #65636).
Security, dependencies and build - **Security** - ReDoS in the validation-error sanitizer fixed (#52120). - FunAudioChat audio bounded to the profiled duration (#57411). - `/v1/systemone` honors `--trust-request-chat-template` (#64503). - Raised floors for filelock, OpenTelemetry, graphql-core and others (#63574). - **Dependencies** - PyTorch stays at 2.14.0. FlashInfer 0.7.3 (#65930). - `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0`, `tokenizers >= 0.23.3`, `timm >= 1.0.30` (#64779); `transformers >= 5.16.1, < 5.23.0` (#64049, #64529); `mistral-common >= 1.13.0` (#64169). - DeepEP 2.1 (#59844); DeepGEMM pin updates (#64411, #64580, #65494); FlashMLA and FlashKDA pins (#61971, #64759). - NIXL 1.5.2 (#64579, #64585); mooncake-transfer-engine 0.3.14 (#65576); Run:ai Model Streamer 0.17.1 (#63174); `fastokens >= 0.3.5` for `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS` (#65679). - ROCm: AITER v0.1.27 → v0.1.28.post1 (#63774, #65937). XPU: PyTorch 2.15 (#63977), triton-xpu 3.9.0 (#65047), vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.17 (#60609). CPU: zentorch 2.14.0.2 (#65669). - **Build** - x86_64 CUDA wheel about 82 MB (about 25%) smaller, kernels unchanged (#65518). - Default CUDA image installs the AWS EFA userspace; the `-efa` image now only adds DeepEP for EFA (#65576); nightly EFA images as `vllm/vllm-openai:efa-nightly` (#64028). - One ROCm build and release pipeline, ROCm 10.0 only (#61939). - Source builds fetch `triton_kernels` from a tarball (#65162) and ship tuned kernel configs in the wheel (#64063). - CUDA `x.yf` arches no longer fall back to a lower minor (#66016).
All breaking changes, deprecations and new defaults - **Model Runner V1 removed** (#63373). - `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` and `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` are gone; setting the env var to anything but `1` fails at startup. - Dropped with it: the V1 logits-processor API (`vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor` is the only interface), the `custom_class` speculative method, `use_heterogeneous_vocab`, `disable_padded_drafter_batch`, `parallel_drafting` outside DFlash/DSpark, PP with `external_launcher`, `NGramPerReqLogitsProcessor`, and x86 CPUs without Triton. - Deprecated: `parallel_drafting`, `capture_torch_profiler`, `enable_layerwise_nvtx_tracing`. - **Default `--block-size` is 64** instead of 16 (#63231). Backends with a preferred block size still override it (ROCm paged attention keeps 16), and an explicit `--block-size` still wins. - **`gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0** when unset with the extensible KV cache on (#56492). An explicit value in (0.8, 1.0) that withholds 1 GiB or more logs a warning (#66704). - **ROCm 7.2** wheels and `-rocm72` images are no longer published (#61939). - **Removed:** - QuTLASS and the `fp_quant` method (#65230). - Marlin INT8/FP8-activation (W4A8) paths and `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE`; use `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` (#65542). - Keye-VL and Keye-VL-1.5 (#64287); `disable_mtp_completeness_check` (#49459); the `refresh_derived_weights` hook (#65914). - **Dependencies:** `huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0` (#64779); `mistral-common >= 1.13.0` (#64169); XPU requires vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.17 (#60609). - **Model and plugin code:** all `process_weights_after_loading` hooks share one signature and the loader runs every module's hook (#57678); config `compute_hash()` replaced by `compile_factors()` / `hash_config()` (#65652). - **API behavior:** - llama3_json no longer streams tool arguments incrementally (#63569). - Canary transcription without `language` returns 400 (#65445). - An empty `tools` array is accepted in both frontends (#65547, #65854). - `/v1/systemone` rejects request-supplied chat templates without `--trust-request-chat-template` (#64503). - LoRA adapters on modules vLLM does not wrap are refused (#63489); misconfigured NCCL weight transfer raises (#57022). - `vllm-rs serve` no longer reads `--data-parallel-rank` from `VLLM_DP_RANK` (#65369). - AITER fused shared experts with MiniMax M3 and DeepSeek V4 need `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` (#61457). - **Still deprecated:** `--mamba-cache-mode` has no effect; its removal was postponed (#64838). - **New defaults:** - Extensible KV cache (#56492); block size 64 (#63231); best-effort NUMA binding (#61258). - Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill at 1024 or more prefill tokens (#63956); MLA decode up-projection before the A2A merge (#64994). - `VLLM_COMPILE_ON_ONE_RANK` (#63247); minimum valid EPLB `num_redundant_experts` (#30614). - HiSparse on the extensible KV cache (#65214); encoder CUDA graphs up to `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget=5120`, eager above (#65227). - TRITON_ATTN on RDNA3/RDNA4 (#60418); MRV2 on non-Triton CPUs (#61995); `float32` Mamba SSM cache for Nemotron Omni (#63218); Zipf routing in `vllm bench forward` (#64167).

json.name: v1.40.3
json.body:
**Enhance**
- Requires `modelscope-hub>=0.7.0`.
- New `modelscope.utils.file_utils.get_hub_cache_root()`; `modelscope.hub.cache_manager` re-exports `get_cache_root` and `resolve_cached_snapshot`. `MS_CACHE_HOME` is normalised to an absolute path when bridged into the hub config.

**Fix**
- `model_file_download(..., local_files_only=True)` no longer calls the API to resolve the default revision, so offline downloads from cache work without network access or credentials.
- `ms clear-cache` lists every resolved target before deleting and delegates to modelscope-hub's scoped cache APIs; cache deletion via `FileSystemCache` goes through the same validated removal, refusing empty identifiers, path traversal, out-of-root targets and symlinked paths.
- `update_local_model` no longer copies models that already live under the legacy model root or the modelscope-hub cache root.
- Hugging Face patch: `hf_hub_download` translates missing files to `EntryNotFoundError` and cache misses to `LocalEntryNotFoundError`, so callers relying on Hugging Face exception types keep working.
- `modelscope.hub.snapshot_download` exports `InvalidParameter` again, preserving the shim module's exception contract.

**Docs**
- Docstrings for the legacy cache-path helpers now state that they describe the legacy layout only and point to `get_hub_cache_root()`, `snapshot_download()` and `resolve_cached_snapshot()`.

## What's Changed
* Offline Download & Cache Cleanup Fixes by @wangxingjun778 in https://github.com/modelscope/modelscope/pull/1844


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/modelscope/modelscope/compare/v1.40.2...v1.40.3

json.body:
# Highlights

*1007 PRs from 257 contributors.*

## New models

| Model | Type | Cookbook |
|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark Open | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Meta/MuseSparkOpen) |
| Beam-1.0 | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Reflection/Beam-1_0) |
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/MiniMax/MiniMax-M3.1) |
| MiniCPM-V 4.7 | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-V-4_7) |
| Kev | LLM / VLM | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Kev/kev) |
| Cosmos3-Nano-Sim (Bimanual, Transfer, Auto) | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/Cosmos/Cosmos3) |
| FastH3 Omni | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3) |
| FLUX.3 Image Klein | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/FLUX/FLUX.3) |
| HY-Nomas | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/HY-Nomas/HY-Nomas) |
| MOSS-Image | Diffusion | [link](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image) |

## What's new

* DeepSeek-V4.1 on GB300 gets up to 1.5x more prefill throughput under load and about 28% lower first-token latency on 32K to 64K prompts ([#44403](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44403), [#45059](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45059), [#45107](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45107)).
* SGLang low-latency mode: the opt-in NVIDIA [megakernel](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega) and AMD [monokernel](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono) plugins run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode as fused persistent kernels, for up to 44% faster single-user decode on GB300 and 75% on MI350X ([#44945](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44945), [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450), [#44353](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44353), [#44621](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44621)).
* MoE models such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and gpt-oss reach the first token 30% to 58% sooner on 8K prompts on H200 ([#43363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43363)).
* Paged Experts (opt-in) runs MoE models larger than GPU memory on a single consumer GPU, up to 30x faster than CPU offload ([#42557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42557), [#45787](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45787)).
* SGLang now runs on Google TPU7x through [SGLang-TorchTPU](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu), a PyTorch-native plugin for TPU.
* You can now serve LoRA adapters on quantized MoE models (FP8 and NVFP4) with a new opt-in LoRA engine ([#45892](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45892)).
* DeepSeek-style MLA models running decode context parallelism can now keep their prefix cache in HiCache file-based L3 storage ([#41187](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41187)).

## To upgrade

```bash
uv pip install --prerelease=allow sglang==0.5.23
```

| Platform | Docker |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA (CUDA 13) | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23` |
| AMD MI35x | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23-rocm10-mi35x` |
| AMD MI30x | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23-rocm10-mi30x` |
| Intel GPU | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23-xpu` |
| Intel CPU | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23-xeon` |
| Google TPU7x (TorchTPU) | `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.1.0-tpu` |

# Full Release Notes

## Speculative Decoding

* [Feat] speculative: Seed rejection-sampling draft proposals for deterministic inference: [#33395](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33395)
* [Fix] observability: Correct speculative FPM timing and decode lengths: [#38711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38711)
* [Perf] spec: Let the FlashAttention backend capture the draft-extend CUDA graph (about 1.5x decode throughput at batch size 1 with a single-layer MoE drafter): [#40762](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40762)
* [Perf] spec-decoding: fuse simulated speculative acceptance tensor preparation: [#41169](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41169)
* [Fix] dsa: Fix ragged seed indices before MTP draft decode: [#42565](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42565)

* [Feat] spec: Let out-of-tree platforms provide their own speculative worker: [#45144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45144)

* [Fix] deepseek-v4: Keep the draft MoE out of the target's expert placement: [#45299](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45299)
* [Perf] [NVIDIA] dspark: Move the host work between DSv4.1 decode graphs into the graphs for the megakernel path: [#45450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45450)

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 chat now follows deepseek-recipe.** Prompts, outputs and the native `/separate_reasoning` and `/parse_function_call` endpoints go through DeepSeek's official encoder, and SGLang's own `encoding_dsv4.py` / `encoding_dsv41.py` are gone. Clients may notice: streamed tool-call arguments arrive in pieces (the first chunk carries `arguments: ""`), so concatenate them as the OpenAI SDK does; tool-call ids use the official `call_00_...` format; V4 reasoning effort follows DeepSeek's official profile and the `dsv4_reasoning_effort_profile` override is removed; a numeric `reasoning_effort` on V4 returns 400; `developer` messages render as system messages; `/parse_function_call` also returns calls to tools outside `tools` with `tool_index` -1; requests that combine `tools` with `continue_final_message` return 400. Output parsing goes through deepseek-recipe when the DeepSeek reasoning or tool-call parser is set; sgl-router and sglang-server keep their Rust parsers for now: [#45315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45315), [#45907](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45907), [#46219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46219)
* **DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder SWA bounded replay is on by default** for supported CUDA configurations, including both PD roles. It is not numerically identical to full prefill. Pass `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` to keep full prefill, for example for RL rollouts whose logprobs must match the trainer: [#44403](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44403), [#45035](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45035)
* **DeepSeek-V4.1 defaults to MegaAttention under PD.** On SM100 / SM103 both PD roles now resolve `flashmla_mega` and the PD handshake checks the KV layout, so prefill and decode must run the same attention backend ([#45075](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45075)). Upgrade prefill and decode together, since an older decode cannot read the new handshake field; pass `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla` on both roles to keep FlashMLA. Aggregated servers keep FlashMLA when attention is tensor-parallel across ranks: [#46263](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46263)
* **The `tokenspeed_mla` attention backend is removed.** `tokenspeed_mla` still starts as a deprecated alias for `cutedsl_mla` with a warning. To switch, pass `--attention-backend cutedsl_mla --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, plus `--speculative-attention-mode decode` with speculative decoding: [#44803](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44803)
* **`--speculative-skip-dp-mlp-sync` is removed.** Launch commands that pass it now fail with an unrecognized-argument error; drop the flag: [#45043](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45043)
* **The `kitchen_int8` diffusion quantization name is removed.** Use `convrot_int8`, deprecated in favor of it since v0.5.22: [#45706](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45706)
* **`SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE` is now ignored without a warning.** It already had no effect because the unified radix tree is the default; drop it from launch scripts: [#45090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45090)
* **Legacy tar-format `.pt` checkpoints no longer load.** The unsafe `weights_only=False` pickle fallback is removed; convert such checkpoints to safetensors or zip-format `.pt` offline: [#42760](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42760)
* **Diffusion HTTP endpoints validate more strictly.** URL values for `upscaling_model_path` and `frame_interpolation_model_path` return 400, an unsupported `response_format` is rejected before generation, and a failed cloud upload returns 502 instead of 400: [#43585](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43585)
* **The first startup of a FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE server takes longer.** Startup autotune now also covers prefill sizes, so a server with no saved tuning results takes longer to become ready (on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x H200, autotune goes from about 41 s to 177 s). Later startups reuse the saved results, and `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` skips tuning: [#43363](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43363)
* **Diffusion PNG responses are larger.** PNG output now defaults to zlib level 0: the same pixels, about 3x the bytes, several times faster to encode. Set `output_compression` to a value other than 75 to pick a level: [#45987](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45987)
* **sgl-router moved to the top-level `sgl-router/` directory.** Builds and scripts that point at `experimental/sgl-router/` must update the path ([#45414](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45414)); `--max-in-flight` is now `--max-inflight-requests`, and the old name still works as an alias: [#44950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44950)

json.body:
## Overview

llama.cpp v1.1.0 adds the Inkling 2 family (base, Mini and DSpark), Domyn Edge 4B, Zaya1 8B, RAON-1-mini and Hy4 flash, splits DFlash speculative decoding into separate draft methods, and deprecates the old `llama_batch` API in favour of `llama_batch_ext`. It brings a large set of TTS and audio models (Kokoro, Zonos3-Mini, tiny-voca, VoxCPM2, MiniMax-Music3, YuE2, Fish S2, Higgs v3/VibeVoice-ASR and Kyutai Hibiki), token-aware chat parsing, named tool choice, automatic per-tensor quantization targeting a bpw or size budget, a slot-scheduling refactor in `llama-server`, a redesigned Llama Chat web UI with voice messages and agent traces, and updates `ggml` to v1.1.1.

### API changes

- llama.h: deprecate the old `llama_batch` API in favour of `llama_batch_ext` and `llama_process` ([#32306](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32306), [#32356](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32356))
- llama.h: add `llama_dflash_variant` and `llama_model_dflash_variant()` for the four DFlash draft heads ([#32016](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32016))
- llama.h: add `llama_model_meta_arr_n()` and `llama_model_meta_arr_str()` to read GGUF string arrays ([#32397](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32397))

### ggml changes

- [v1.1.0](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v1.1.0): ggml v1.1.0 extends the graph API for new model families, strengthens scheduler and backend behavior, and brings broad performance work across all backends. The API gains gated-delta-net replay, flash-attention indexed bias, ordered asynchronous host input copies, and scheduler scratch reservation, plus new SLEEP and SIGMOID_BACK operators. Core adds BF16 coverage for more operations, faster quantization and math helpers, and new CPU quant kernels, while backends add stream-k matmul, chunked command buffers, NVFP4, CONV_2D acceleration, wider FP8/BF16 support, and many tuning and correctness fixes.
- [v1.1.1](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v1.1.1): ggml v1.1.1 lands Hexagon 2.0 with INT-HMX W8A8 matmul, automatic F32 to F16 lowering and generic DMA pipelines, and brings a CUDA FlashAttention data-loading refactor, a SYCL gated-delta-net ESIMD kernel with fused recurrent convolutions, small-K Metal mat-vec tuning, and a WebGPU log1p for softplus. It also adds the TANH backward pass, OpenVINO decode and op-test fixes, and 16-head lightning-indexer support on CUDA.

json.description: An open platform for training, serving, and evaluating large language models. Release repo for Vicuna and Chatbot Arena.

json.name: Release v0.2.36
json.body:
## Highlights
- Added SGLang worker for vision language models, lower latency and higher throughput https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/pull/2928
- Vision langauge WebUI https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/pull/2960
- OpenAI-compatible API server now supports image input https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/pull/2928
- Added LightLLM worker for higher throughput https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/blob/main/docs/lightllm_integration.md

json.name: PyTorch 2.15.0 Release
json.body:
# PyTorch 2.15.0 Release Notes - [Highlights](#highlights) - [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes) - [Deprecations](#deprecations) - [New Features](#new-features) - [Improvements](#improvements) - [Bug fixes](#bug-fixes) - [Performance](#performance) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Security](#security) - [Developers](#developers) # Highlights
Rewritten NCCL backend becomes the default, with a flight recorder that dumps on hangs and TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or nccl-legacy as rollback paths
One-sided transports for torch.distributed, with a NIXL backend and CUDA-graph-capturable transfers
FSDP2 and pipelining gain finer memory and communication control, with fp32 for precision-sensitive parameters, CUDA-graph-captured gradient accumulation, and gradient reduction overlapped with compute
Faster 4-bit (NVFP4) LLM decoding on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs through fewer, better-overlapped kernel launches in NVGEMM
Apple Silicon gains FP8 and faster decode, with float8_e4m3fn and _scaled_mm, a new grouped_mm with a decode fast path (1.32–1.34x tokens/s on MoE decode), and public torch.mps.Stream APIs
Broader platform support with FlyDSL kernels on AMD gfx950, Tensor Data Mover support for gfx1250 (MI450), ROCm 10.0 wheels, simpler SYCL kernel authoring and multi-GPU profiling on Intel GPUs, CUDA 13.2 as the default wheel with CUDA 13.4 alongside it, and torch.compile on Python 3.15
For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release. # Backwards Incompatible Changes ## Python Frontend ### `import torch` can no longer be re-executed in the same process, including via `importlib.reload(torch)` (#194654) `importlib.reload(torch)` and `del sys.modules["torch"]` + re-import now raise, as does retrying `import torch` after it failed. Re-running the module body was already unsafe in exactly the same way as the retry, so the new check does not distinguish the two. Normal use is unaffected: a successful import leaves `torch` in `sys.modules` so the body never re-runs, and re-entrant imports from a backend extension during autoload still short-circuit on `sys.modules` without reaching the check. Version 2.14: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # RuntimeError: Only a single TORCH_LIBRARY can be used to register the namespace triton; ... # (re-importing after a failed `import torch` failed with similarly misleading errors or could segfault) ``` Version 2.15: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # ImportError: `torch` can only be initialized once per process, so this module cannot # be imported again: neither via `importlib.reload(torch)`, nor by re-importing after # a failed `import torch`. ``` ### Nested tensors are no longer allowlisted for `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` (#194380) Nested jagged and strided nested tensors are no longer on the default `weights_only` allowlist. Loading a checkpoint that contains one with `weights_only=True` (the default) now fails with `Unsupported global: GLOBAL torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor._rebuild_njt was not an allowed global by default` (or `GLOBAL torch._utils._rebuild_nested_tensor` for strided nested tensors). To load checkpoints containing nested tensors, allow them explicitly with `torch.serialization.safe_globals` (see below), or use `weights_only=False` for trusted files. Version 2.14: ```python loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) # works ``` Version 2.15: ```python from torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor import _rebuild_njt, NestedTensor with torch.serialization.safe_globals([_rebuild_njt, NestedTensor]): loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) ``` ### Operators called through `torch.ops.*` and `torch._C._dispatch_call_boxed` now use PyTorch's own warning and exception translation instead of pybind11's (#193451) We make `torch.ops.*` calls go through the same exception and warning translation as the rest of the library. This means that some exception translation that used to be handled by pybind is now handled natively. User-defined pybind exception translation is thus lost. Restoring it may be done in a future release as part of a broader exception handler improvement. In addition, `TORCH_WARN` warnings from these operators now reach Python's `warnings` module, so they raise when warnings are turned into errors (`-W error`). `std::out_of_range` still becomes `IndexError` (#195713). Version 2.14: ```python # C++ op: throw std::invalid_argument("bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: # pybind11 translation ... ``` Version 2.15: ```python # C++ op: TORCH_CHECK_VALUE(false, "bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: ... # TORCH_WARN from the op is now a Python warning with warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter("ignore") torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) ``` ## Autograd ### Selective activation checkpointing now saves, rather than recomputes, the outputs of operators with an ordered effect unless the policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` (#196956) In eager mode, if a `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts` policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE` for a non-aliasing operator with an ordered effect (e.g. via `register_effect(torch.library.EffectType.ORDERED)`), that choice is now overridden and its outputs are saved, so the side effect is no longer replayed during backward. This can increase activation memory. To keep the 2.14 behavior, return `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` for that operator. Operators in the `c10d` namespace are excluded. Under `torch.compile`, `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` on an effectful operator now raises at compile time: `RuntimeError: AOTAutograd does not support MUST_RECOMPUTE for effectful operations because forward effects cannot join the backward effect-token chain.` Use a save policy instead. ```python policy = lambda ctx, op, *args, **kwargs: CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE checkpoint(fn, x, use_reentrant=False, context_fn=lambda: create_selective_checkpoint_contexts(policy)) # 2.14: an effectful op in fn runs twice; 2.15: once (use CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE to replay) ``` ## Distributed (c10d) ### The `nccl` backend now uses a rewritten, cleaned-up NCCL implementation by default (#192281, #192895, #193237, #193241) `backend="nccl"` (also the default CUDA backend of `init_process_group()`) now creates the new implementation. The legacy implementation is available as `backend="nccl-legacy"` for this release only: **`nccl-legacy` and `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` will be removed in the next release**, so migrate to `nccl` or `nccl-lazy`. Use `nccl` (eager initialization) by default. Use `nccl-lazy` when you need independent point-to-point communicators: collectives run on one eagerly created communicator, and each send/recv peer pair gets its own lazily created communicator and stream, so concurrent P2P to different peers can overlap (as in the legacy backend). Differences from the legacy backend: - Communicators are created eagerly in `init_process_group()`/`new_group()`, allocating GPU memory even for unused groups. - Each group is bound to one CUDA device: `device_id`, else `LOCAL_RANK % torch.cuda.device_count()` (or the global rank modulo the device count); `torch.cuda.set_device()` is not used. Tensors on another GPU fail with `Expected tensor on cuda:X but found tensor on cuda:Y` or `ProcessGroupNCCL is bound to device cuda:X but an operation was issued on cuda:Y`. Pass `device_id` if needed; several GPUs per process requires `nccl-legacy`. - `dist.get_backend_impl(...)` returns the new backend class, so `isinstance(..., ProcessGroupNCCL)` is `False` and legacy-only methods such as `comm_split_count()` are missing. - An async `all_gather`'s `work.get_future()` value is the list of per-rank outputs, not a one-element list holding a stacked tensor; read the output list passed to `all_gather` instead (works on both backends). To temporarily restore the legacy behavior in 2.15, set `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` on every rank before creating the process group, or use `nccl-legacy`: Version 2.14: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl") # ProcessGroupNCCL ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # new implementation dist.init_process_group("nccl-lazy", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # independent P2P communicators dist.init_process_group("nccl-legacy") # legacy implementation, removed in the next release ``` ## Distributed Checkpointing ### Distributed checkpoint metadata now records tensor strides, so checkpoints saved with PyTorch 2.15 cannot be loaded by PyTorch 2.14 or earlier (#194251) `TensorProperties` gains an optional `strides` field in the pickled `.metadata` file. In older versions `dcp.load` raises a `CheckpointException` reporting `too many values to unpack (expected 5)`. There is no flag to write the old format. Version 2.14 (loading a 2.15 checkpoint): ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # CheckpointException: ... too many values to unpack (expected 5) ``` Version 2.15: ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # loads 2.14 and 2.15 checkpoints ``` ## Distributed FSDP2 ### With `MixedPrecisionPolicy(reduce_dtype=None)`, `fully_shard` now accumulates and reduces gradients in the parameter's `grad_dtype` (its original dtype by default) instead of in `param_dtype` (#194434) **This is BC-breaking**: `mp_policy.reduce_dtype=None` no longer defaults to `mp_policy.param_dtype`. * [popular case] fp32 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=bf16)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 (2x reduce-scatter bytes) * [rare case] bf16 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=fp32)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 How to deal with BC: explicitly set `mp_policy.reduce_dtype`. In grad accumulation (no reduce-scatter), the unsharded param's `.grad` always holds the accumulated value, visible via `model.parameters()` while unsharded. Before this change, `.grad` was `None` when `reduce_dtype` was set and differed from `param_dtype` (FSDP kept the sum in a hidden `reduce_dtype` buffer). Version 2.14: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in bf16 ``` Version 2.15: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in fp32 # to keep the 2.14 behavior, set reduce_dtype explicitly mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16, reduce_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) ``` ## Distributed Pipelining ### `torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p` is renamed to `pipeline_per_edge_p2p` and now uses one communicator per directed rank-to-rank edge (#196666) The old names were removed with no alias: setting the attribute raises `AttributeError: torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p does not exist`, and `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_DIRECTION_P2P` is silently ignored. Version 2.14: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_edge_p2p = True # or TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_EDGE_P2P=1 ``` ## Profiler ### C++ stack traces are now symbolized with `dladdr` instead of `addr2line` by default (#195462) `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE` now defaults to on, since `addr2line` is slow and can hang. C++ frames in `TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1` errors and CUDA memory snapshots now show the library path and offset, plus the symbol name only if exported (otherwise `??`). To restore `addr2line`, set `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0` or `TORCH_SYMBOLIZE_MODE=addr2line`. ```bash TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1 TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0 python train.py ``` ### CUDA memory snapshots record the allocator's `mallocWithAddress` tag in a new `internal_metadata` field instead of appending it to `user_metadata` (#193432) `user_metadata` in `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` trace entries is now exactly what was set with `torch.cuda.memory._set_memory_metadata` (which now also accepts a dict). Tools that searched `user_metadata` for `mallocWithAddress` must read `internal_metadata` instead. ```python # 2.14 tagged = [e for e in trace if "mallocWithAddress" in e["user_metadata"]] # 2.15 tagged = [e for e in trace if e.get("internal_metadata") == "mallocWithAddress"] ``` ### Remove the deprecated `FunctionEvent.metadata_json` property (#198265) Accessing it now raises `AttributeError: 'FunctionEvent' object has no attribute 'metadata_json'`, and the `metadata_json` constructor argument is removed. Use `FunctionEvent.metadata`, a dict populated when `_ExperimentalConfig(expose_kineto_event_metadata=True)` is set (not the deprecated `event_metadata`). ```python metadata = event.metadata_json # 2.14: JSON string metadata = event.metadata # 2.15: dict[str, Any] or None ``` ### Rename the experimental CUPTI monitor profiler backend to Cuspy, without aliases for the old names (#195881) In `_ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config=...)`, `"cupti_monitor"` is now `"cuspy"` and `"cupti_monitor_async_export"` is now `"cuspy_async_export"`; old names silently fall back to the default Kineto backend. `prof.take_pending_cupti_export()` is now `take_pending_cuspy_export()` (the old name raises `AttributeError`). Prefer the new `torch.profiler.CuspyConfig`. ```python # 2.14 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cupti_monitor"}') # 2.15 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cuspy"}') ``` ## Dynamo ### Higher-order ops now reject input mutation and aliasing in their bodies unless the op opts in (#185738) Before, Dynamo let any higher-order op body mutate or alias its inputs by default. Ops that do not implement those semantics could silently produce invalid graphs. Mutation and aliasing are now off by default. The built-in wrappers that support them (`wrap`, checkpoint, `autograd.Function`, autocast/set-grad wrappers) opt in. A `flex_attention` `mask_mod` may read captured views but must not mutate inputs or return aliases. Under `fullgraph=True`, unsupported mutation or aliasing raises `Encountered input mutation during higher order op tracing` or `Encountered aliasing during higher order op tracing`; otherwise, Dynamo graph breaks and falls back to eager execution. Rewrite the higher-order op body to avoid mutation or aliasing. For example, rewrite an in-place `flex_attention` score modifier as an out-of-place operation: Version 2.14: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): score.add_(1) return score.clone() ``` Version 2.15: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): return score + 1 ``` ## Inductor ### `torch.compiler.nested_compile_region(options=...)` now accepts only an allowlist of Inductor config patches (#195864, #195865) Patches passed through `get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches=..., bw_inductor_config_patches=...)` used to accept any `torch._inductor.config` key, though many were silently ignored. Only `fallback_by_default` and `max_autotune` are now accepted; other keys raise `ValueError: Inductor config key '' is not supported in forward nested compile-region options` (or `backward`). Apply other options to the whole compiled function. Patch dictionaries are now snapshotted when the options are created, so later mutation has no effect, and the default no longer implicitly sets `triton.autotune_at_compile_time=True`. Version 2.14: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` Version 2.15: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"max_autotune": True}) compiled = torch.compile(fn, options={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` ### `torch.compiler.precompile` is now a module instead of a callable; capture with `torch.compiler.precompile.capture(...)` and reload with `torch.compiler.precompile.load(...)` (#197993, #198135, #198213) Calling `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` now raises `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable`. `capture(fn, *, artifact_path, cache_path)` returns a context manager that you call once inside the `with` block; it writes both files when the block exits cleanly (or on `cap.save()`), and `load` now takes those paths. `decompositions=` moves to `tracer=MakeFxTracer(decompositions=...)`. Version 2.14: ```python python_code, cache = torch.compiler.precompile(lambda m, x: m(x), model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load(python_code, cache) ``` Version 2.15: ```python with torch.compiler.precompile.capture(lambda m, x: m(x), artifact_path="m.py", cache_path="m.cache") as cap: cap(model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache") ``` ## Composability ### Under functionalization, a regenerated output of `split`, `split_with_sizes` or `unbind` is now rebuilt as a single `slice` or `select` of its base, so its `grad_fn` is `SliceBackward0`/`SelectBackward0` instead of `SplitBackward0`/`SplitWithSizesBackward0`/`UnbindBackward0` (#194037) This greatly reduces compile time for code that mutates many `split()` views (for example 32s to 15s with 128 views). Gradients are unchanged, but the in-place error now names the new op with output index 0: `RuntimeError: Output 0 of Select is a view and is being modified inplace.` Code that inspects `grad_fn` names, matches the old error text, or pattern-matches `split`/`unbind` nodes in functionalized graphs needs updating. There is no option to restore the previous behavior. Version 2.14: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) # f returns base.unbind(0)[1] after base.add_(1) >>> out.grad_fn ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) >>> out.grad_fn ``` ## Release Engineering ### PyPI wheels now ship with CUDA 13.2, and CUDA 12.6 and CUDA 13.0 wheels are no longer published (#196249, #198913) The default PyPI wheel moves from CUDA 13.0 to CUDA 13.2. The 2.15 wheels are `cu132` and `cu134`; `cu126` and `cu130` are no longer built. CUDA 13 wheels need NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and a GPU of Turing (`sm_75`) or newer, so Maxwell, Pascal and Volta GPUs and hosts with a CUDA 12.x driver should stay on 2.14. Version 2.15: ```bash # PyPI wheel now uses CUDA 13.2 pip install torch # CUDA 13.4 wheels pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu134 # To stay on CUDA 12.6 or CUDA 13.0, pin PyTorch 2.14: pip install torch==2.14.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126 # or cu130 ``` ### Python 3.10 wheels are no longer published (#198233, #199398) PyTorch 2.15 raises the minimum supported Python version for binaries to 3.11: no `cp310` wheels are built for `torch` or the Triton wheels, and CI no longer tests on Python 3.10. On Python 3.10, `pip` cannot find a 2.15 wheel. Upgrade to Python 3.11 or newer, or stay on PyTorch 2.14. Version 2.14: ```bash python3.10 -m pip install torch # cp310 wheel available ``` Version 2.15: ```bash python3.11 -m pip install torch==2.15.0 # Python 3.11 through 3.15 (including 3.14t and 3.15t) ``` ### ROCm wheels move to ROCm 7.14 and 10.0; ROCm 7.2 wheels and gfx900/gfx906 kernels are dropped (#194919) gfx900 (MI25) and gfx906 (MI50/MI60, Radeon VII) users can stay on 2.14 (`rocm7.2`) or build from source with those targets in `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH`. ```bash pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.14 # or rocm10.0 ``` ### Linux CUDA wheels no longer depend on the cuRAND library (#194850) PyTorch only uses the cuRAND device API, so `torch` no longer links `libcurand`, no longer preloads it on `import torch`, and the wheel's CUDA requirements no longer include cuRAND. Extensions or libraries that call the cuRAND host API (for example `curandCreateGenerator`) and relied on `pip install torch` bringing in the cuRAND library can fail to load `libcurand.so` and must now install it themselves. Version 2.15: ```bash pip install torch pip install "cuda-toolkit[curand]==13.2.2" # match the toolkit version of your wheel ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.histc(..., out=...)` on CUDA now raises an error when `out` does not have the same dtype as the input (#196100) CUDA used to silently cast into any `out` dtype. It now matches CPU and MPS and rejects mismatches, even widening ones. Compute without `out` and cast instead. Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0, out=int64_out) # silently truncated ``` Version 2.15: ```python RuntimeError: torch.histogram: input tensor and hist tensor should have the same dtype, but got input float and hist long int >>> int64_out.copy_(torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0)) # workaround ``` ### On CUDA, cuBLAS and cuBLASLt workspaces are now allocated for each operation instead of being cached per handle and stream (#194311) Graphs captured separately on one stream could share the cached workspace and fail on replay with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Workspaces are now freed after each op, so `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` excludes them and the handle from `torch.cuda.current_blas_handle()` has no ATen workspace attached. Set `TORCH_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CACHE=1` to restore caching (unsafe with multiple graphs on one stream). `TORCH_CUBLASLT_UNIFIED_WORKSPACE` now only takes effect with caching enabled. ROCm has a matching change (#196920). Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.mm(a, a, out=out) >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before > 0 # workspace stays allocated True ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before # freed after the op 0 ``` ## CPU (AArch64) ### Float32 `torch.sin` and `torch.cos` on Arm CPUs (NEON and SVE) now use SLEEF's 3.5-ULP kernels instead of the 1.0-ULP kernels, matching the accuracy of the x86 AVX2 implementation and running 1.7x-2.4x faster on Neoverse V1/V2 (#196315) Float32 `sin` and `cos` results on Arm can now differ from earlier releases in the last bits. Bit-for-bit comparisons against stored golden outputs, `torch.equal`, or `torch.testing.assert_close` with `rtol=0, atol=0` may fail; default `assert_close` tolerances are unaffected. There is no switch to restore the previous kernels; if you need tighter accuracy, compute in float64 and cast back. Version 2.14: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 1 ULP ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 2 ULP >>> x.double().cos().float() # workaround: correctly rounded ``` ## MPS ### The MPS backend now requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer (#199261, #200290) macOS 14 has reached end of life, so its MPS workarounds were removed. On macOS 14, `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` returns `False` and allocating on `mps` raises the error below. To keep using MPS, stay on PyTorch 2.14 or upgrade macOS; CPU builds still run on older macOS. C++ extensions: `at::mps::MacOSVersion::MACOS_14_4` was removed. ```python >>> torch.ones(2, device="mps") # 2.15 on macOS 14 RuntimeError: The MPS backend is supported on macOS 15.0+. Current OS version can be queried using `sw_vers` ``` ## XPU ### Remove the `allocator` property from `torch.xpu.MemPool`, aligning with other accelerators (#192041) `torch.xpu.MemPool` no longer exposes the allocator it was constructed with, so `pool.allocator` now raises `AttributeError`. Keep your own reference to the allocator instead; passing one to the `MemPool` constructor is unchanged. Before: ```python pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(allocator.allocator()) my_allocator = pool.allocator ``` After: ```python my_allocator = allocator.allocator() pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(my_allocator) ``` ## Complex Frontend ### Ops that are undefined for complex inputs now raise `TypeError` instead of `RuntimeError` (#192350) This covers order-dependent ops (`sort`, `argsort`, `topk`, `argmax`/`argmin`, `max`/`min` with `dim`, `maximum`/`minimum`, `fmax`/`fmin`, `aminmax`), `isposinf`/`isneginf`, `view_as_real`/`imag` on real tensors, and `view_as_complex` on complex tensors, matching Python (`1j < 2j` is a `TypeError`). `except RuntimeError:` no longer catches these; catch `(RuntimeError, TypeError)`. Ops not yet implemented for a dtype (e.g. `rad2deg`, `nansum`, `heaviside` on complex, `topk`/`argmax` on bool) now raise `NotImplementedError`, which `except RuntimeError:` still catches. Full `max()`/`min()`/`amax`/`amin` are unchanged. ```python torch.sort(torch.randn(3, dtype=torch.cfloat)) # 2.14: RuntimeError: Sort does not support complex dtypes on CPU # 2.15: TypeError: Sort does not support complex dtypes on CPU ``` # Deprecations ## Optimizer ### Passing a bare `set` of parameters to an optimizer is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning`; it will become an error in a future release (#198710) Set iteration order can change between runs, so optimizer state could silently mismatch parameters on reload. The warning reads: `optimizer parameters need to be organized in ordered collections, but the ordering of tensors in sets will change between runs. Please use a list instead.` ```python opt = torch.optim.Adam(set(model.parameters())) # 2.15: FutureWarning opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(model.parameters())) # recommended ``` ## Linear Algebra Frontend ### MAGMA is deprecated for LU factorization with pivoting on CUDA: `torch.linalg.lu_factor`, `torch.linalg.lu`, and the ops that use it internally (`torch.linalg.solve`, `torch.linalg.inv`, `torch.linalg.det`, `torch.linalg.slogdet`) now always use cuSOLVER (#190661) This only affects code that sets `torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("magma")`: pivoted LU now uses cuSOLVER anyway; a new built-in batched LU kernel replaces MAGMA's for large batches. When MAGMA is preferred, the first call warns: `linalg.lu_factor: MAGMA, as a linear algebra backend, is deprecated and will be removed in future releases.` `pivot=False` still uses MAGMA when it is preferred. To avoid the warning, use the default or cuSOLVER backend. ```python torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("magma") LU, pivots = torch.linalg.lu_factor(A) # 2.14: MAGMA; 2.15: cuSOLVER + UserWarning torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library("default") # recommended ``` ## Profiler ### `torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof`, `parse_nvprof_trace` and `EnforceUnique` are deprecated and will be removed in PyTorch 2.17 (#198396) `nvprof` does not support recent GPUs. They now emit a `FutureWarning` such as `` `torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof` is deprecated and will be removed in PyTorch 2.17. `` Use `torch.profiler.profile` or Nsight Systems with `torch.autograd.profiler.emit_nvtx()`. ```python events = torch.autograd.profiler.load_nvprof("trace.prof") # 2.14 with torch.profiler.profile() as prof: # 2.15 run_workload() ``` ### `FunctionEvent.event_metadata` is deprecated in favor of `FunctionEvent.metadata` (#198405) `metadata` is a typed `dict[str, Any]` with everything `event_metadata` had. Accessing `event_metadata` emits `FutureWarning: `event_metadata` is deprecated. Use `metadata` instead.` ```python grid = event.event_metadata.grid # 2.14 grid = event.metadata["grid"] # 2.15 ``` ## Inductor ### Deprecate `torch._inductor.config.triton.use_block_ptr` because Triton removed its block-pointer API (#191007) With a Triton that no longer provides block pointers, `use_block_ptr=True` is now a no-op that falls back to the default indexing path with a one-time `FutureWarning: config.triton.use_block_ptr=True but the installed Triton no longer provides the block-pointer frontend API`, instead of failing with `CompilationError: ... Block pointers have been removed in favor of the tensor descriptor API`. Use tensor descriptors instead. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.triton.use_block_ptr = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python torch._inductor.config.triton.use_tensor_descriptor = True ``` ### Deprecate the no-op `torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm` and `torch._inductor.config.mixed_mm_choice` settings (#193721) These settings have been ignored since the tuned `mixed_mm` path was removed. Reading or setting either now emits a one-time `FutureWarning` such as `torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm is deprecated and does not do anything`. `autoheuristic_collect.mixed_mm` and `autoheuristic_use.mixed_mm` were removed, and `"mixed_mm"` is no longer the `TORCHINDUCTOR_AUTOHEURISTIC_USE` default. Delete these settings from your code. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.use_mixed_mm = True # silently ignored ``` Version 2.15: ```python # FutureWarning; delete the line ``` ### Rename `torch._inductor.config.benchmark_epilogue_fusion` to `benchmark_template_fusion` and `max_epilogue_benchmarked_choices` to `max_template_fusion_benchmarked_choices` (#198430) The settings also cover prologue fusion, so the old names were misleading. The old names remain as deprecated aliases that emit a one-time `FutureWarning`. The environment variable is now `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_TEMPLATE_FUSION`; `TORCHINDUCTOR_BENCHMARK_EPILOGUE_FUSION` is still read as a fallback. Version 2.14: ```python torch._inductor.config.benchmark_epilogue_fusion = False ``` Version 2.15: ```python torch._inductor.config.benchmark_template_fusion = False ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.cuda.graph_annotations.clear_kernel_annotations()` is deprecated and now emits a `FutureWarning` (#195398) The CUDA graph kernel annotation registry now cleans up after itself: annotations are rekeyed to the executable graph when it is instantiated and dropped when that graph is destroyed. A global clear also discards annotations for graphs that are still live. Remove the call, and reset or delete a graph to drop its annotations. Version 2.14: ```python annotations = get_kernel_annotations() clear_kernel_annotations() ``` Version 2.15: ```python annotations = get_kernel_annotations() # No clear needed; g's annotations are dropped when g is reset or destroyed. ``` # New Features ## torch.nn - Add `torch.nn.functional.scaled_addmm` and in-place `scaled_addmm_`, which compute `beta * input + alpha * scaled_mm(mat1, mat2)` in a single cuBLASLt GEMM on CUDA with the same scaling recipes as `scaled_mm`; also supported under `torch.compile` (#195409, #195410) ## Optimizer - Add `torch.optim.functional`, a public module of functional optimizers (`adam`, `adamw`, `sgd`, `muon` and others) that run the same implementations as the optimizer classes while the caller manages parameters, gradients and state (#194986) ## Autograd - Add `ctx.input_grad_buffers` to custom `torch.autograd.Function` backward, exposing the engine's gradient accumulation buffers (or `None` when unavailable) so a fused kernel can accumulate an input's gradient in place and return `None` for it. `torch.compile` uses it for coalesced collectives and `batch_isend_irecv` (#193892) ## Profiler - Kineto source now lives in `third_party/kineto` instead of a git submodule (#198648) - Remove the ignored `profiler_metrics` and `profiler_measure_per_kernel` `_ExperimentalConfig` arguments (now a `TypeError`), and deprecate the no-op `adjust_profiler_step` option (#198262, #193042) ## FX - Fix type annotations on `Tracer(autowrap_modules=...)` and `CodeGen.process_inputs` (#195467, #188287) ## Inductor - Add `DeviceInterface` and `DeviceOpOverrides` extension points for out-of-tree accelerator backends (#190326, #190614, #192896, #193908, #190615) - Add declarative `implies` support to Inductor/Dynamo `Config` (#196663) ## Ahead-Of-Time Inductor (AOTI) - Add `DeviceOpOverrides.aten_device_type()` so backends provide their ATen device type to AOTInductor C++ codegen (#193904) ## C++ Frontend - `c10::List` iterators satisfy `std::random_access_iterator`, and `List::emplace` now constructs a `T` (#196002) ## Developer Experience - Add `spin test` to run `pytest` or `test/run_test.py` like CI (#198649) ## Build Frontend - Add an opt-in `USE_CMAKE_INSTRUMENTATION=1` build option to collect build metrics (CMake >= 4.3) (#189455) - Turn off `USE_FLASH_ATTENTION` automatically when no target CUDA architecture is sm80 or newer (#194502) - Fix the misspelled `CUDA_LIMIT_GPU_ARCHITECTURE` in CUDA architecture autodetection (#195695) - Honor `USE_MIMALLOC=OFF` on Windows and AArch64 (#199064) - Fix the FlashAttention CUDA build on Windows with MSVC in C++20 mode (#197382) ## Release Engineering - Move the CD wheel build scripts under `.ci/wheel/` (`.ci/manywheel/` to `.ci/wheel/linux/`, `.ci/macwheel/` to `.ci/wheel/mac/`, and the Windows pipeline to `.ci/wheel/windows/`) and share one `numpy` build pin (#189275) - Add a native-AOT stage to CUDA builds that exports CuTeDSL and Triton kernels ahead of time and embeds them into `libtorch_cuda`. The stage skips itself when it does not apply (for example CUDA older than 13 or no supported GPU architecture), but once it decides to export, a missing `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` (or Triton, installable with `scripts/install_triton_wheel.sh`) is a hard error; set `TORCH_NATIVE_AOT=0` to skip the stage (#194243, #196747, #196507) - Fix the CMake C and C++ compiler flag checks sharing one cache variable, so a result for one language could be reused for the other; the generated `HAS_` variables are now prefixed `HAS_C` and `HAS_CXX` (#197614) - Add a persistent `[no-ci]` PR title prefix that skips build, test and lint jobs, and make `@pytorchbot merge -i` ignore current failures across every PR in a ghstack stack (#196534, #197143) ## CUDA - Update the bundled CUTLASS to v4.8.0 and CUTLASS-Operators to v0.3.0 (#198179) ## CPU (AArch64) - Add the `AT_VEC_CUSTOM_MATH` compile definition, which hides the built-in vectorized math functions on AVX2, AVX512, NEON and SVE256 builds so that a vectorized math library other than SLEEF can be plugged in (#197419) ## MPS - Fix building with clang 16 and Apple clang 15 (#199115) - Fix building with a Metal 4 toolchain against older macOS SDKs, and deprecation warnings with the macOS 27 SDK (#196104, #197200) - `at::mps::MPSProfiler` `begin*`/`end*` methods take the `MPSStream*`; stream-less `begin*` overloads are deprecated (#192525, #193611) - Fix macOS builds failing on SDKs that lack the Metal 4 cooperative-tensor APIs (#195302) - Fix stale embedded Metal shaders in incremental macOS builds (#196202) - Fix MPS shader includes in editable installs (#195295) ## ROCm - `torch.utils.cpp_extension.ROCM_VERSION` now uses the ROCm SDK version instead of the HIP runtime version, and `collect_env` reports both (#194985, #193602) ## XPU - Build XPU with pure SYCL compilation and support Clang as the host compiler; expose `USE_SYCLTLA` and enable oneMKL sparse in the build system (#194185, #198720, #196387, #198200) - Upgrade oneDNN to v3.13 (#196712) ## Caffe2 - Fix source builds with CUDA 13.3 (#194659)

json.name: TensorFlow 2.21.0
json.body:
# Release 2.21.0

## TensorFlow

### Breaking Changes

* Support for Python 3.9 has been removed starting with TF 2.21.
* The TensorBoard (TB) dependency has been removed starting with TF 2.21.

### Major Features and Improvements

* `tf.lite`
    * Adds int8 and int16x8 support for SQRT operator.
    * Adds int16x8 support for EQUAL and NOT_EQUAL operators.
    * Adds support for int2 type.
    * Adds support for int2/int4 in tfl.cast .
    * Adds support for SRQ int2 in tfl.fully_connected.
    * Adds support for int4 in tfl.slice.
    * Adds support for uint4 type.

*  `tf.image`
    * Adds JPEG XL support in decode_image.

### Bug Fixes and Other Changes

* `tf.data`
    * Adds `NoneTensorSpec` to the public API so that `None`s in `element_spec`
      can be identified via `isinstance(..., tf.NoneTensorSpec)`.

Apache MXNet (incubating) 1.9.1 is a maintenance release incorporating important bug fixes and performance improvements. All users of Apache MXNet (incubating) 1.9.0 are advised to upgrade.
