json.name: JAX v0.12.1
json.body:
* New features
  * Pallas APIs are now available under `jax.pallas` (`jax.pallas`,
    `jax.pallas.tpu`, `jax.pallas.tpu_sc`, `jax.pallas.mosaic_gpu`, and
    `jax.pallas.fuser`, via explicit `import jax.pallas`). Existing imports from
    `jax.experimental.pallas` remain valid, while `triton` and `ops` stay under
    `jax.experimental.pallas`. See the Pallas changelog for Pallas-specific
    changes.
  * Added a keyword-only `with_logs` option to `jax.grad` and
    `jax.value_and_grad`, returning backward-pass logs alongside
    gradients without calling `jax.vjp` directly. With `with_logs=True`,
    `grad` returns `(grad, logs)` (or `(grad, aux, logs)` when `has_aux=True`),
    and `value_and_grad` returns `(val, (grad, logs))` (or
    `((val, aux), (grad, logs))`).
  * Added `jax.avals` (along with `Mesh.axes` and `AbstractMesh.axes`) for
    concise shorthand construction of abstract array types (`ShapedArray`) with
    optional sharding annotations, such as `f32[3@X]` and `f32[()]`.
  * On Python 3.14 and later, `jax.debug.print` now accepts PEP 750
    template strings (for example, `jax.debug.print(t"hello {x}")`)
    (#41565).
  * Added `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X3` and `F8E4M3FN_F8E4M3FN_F32_X4` to
    `jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset` (and `jax_default_matmul_precision`)
    for emulating `bfloat16` precision matrix multiplications on `bfloat16` or
    `float32` inputs using 3 or 4 `float8_e4m3fn` products accumulated in
    `float32`.
  * Added CPU support for `jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset.F16_F16_F32`, fixing
    `jax.nn.dot_product_attention` with `implementation="xla"` and
    `float16` inputs under `jit` and `grad` on CPU.
  * Added `jax.lax.fma` and `jax.lax.fmuladd` for fused
    multiply-add (`a * b + c`). `fma` performs a single-rounding fused
    multiply-add where supported; `fmuladd` uses fused multiply-add when
    available and falls back safely otherwise (#23919).
    `jax.lax.polynomial` now uses `fmuladd` for floating-point evaluation.
  * Added `jax.lax.sinpi`, `jax.lax.cospi`, and
    `jax.lax.tanpi`, which compute `sin(pi * x)`, `cos(pi * x)`, and
    `tan(pi * x)` more accurately than multiplying by `pi` first. They return
    exact values at integers and half-integers and stay accurate for large
    inputs. Window functions (`jax.numpy.blackman`,
    `jax.numpy.hamming`, `jax.numpy.hanning`),
    `jax.scipy.signal.stft`, `jax.scipy.special.fresnel`, and
    Lanczos `jax.image.resize` now use them for better accuracy.
  * Added `jax.lax.asinpi`, `jax.lax.acospi`,
    `jax.lax.atanpi`, and `jax.lax.atan2pi`, which compute the
    inverse trigonometric functions divided by `pi` (`asin(x) / pi`,
    `acos(x) / pi`, `atan(x) / pi`, and `atan2(x, y) / pi`).
  * Added `jax.lax.exp2m1` and `jax.lax.log2p1`, which compute
    `2**x - 1` and `log2(1 + x)` without losing precision near `x = 0`.
  * Added `jax.scipy.special.gammaincinv` and
    `jax.scipy.special.gammainccinv`, the inverses of the regularized
    lower and upper incomplete gamma functions, with gradients with respect to
    both arguments (#5350).
  * Added `jax.scipy.special.jn`, `jax.scipy.special.yn`,
    `jax.scipy.special.iv`, and `jax.scipy.special.kn`, providing
    accurate evaluation of integer-order Bessel functions and modified Bessel
    functions of the first and second kind (for static integer orders, with
    support for real and complex inputs and automatic differentiation).
  * Added `jax.scipy.special.ndtri_exp`, the inverse of
    `jax.scipy.special.log_ndtr` (`ndtri(exp(y))` without underflow or
    cancellation in log-probability space), supporting accurate forward-,
    reverse-, and higher-order differentiation.
  * `jax.numpy.histogram_bin_edges` and `jax.numpy.histogram` now
    accept `bins="sqrt"` and `bins="sturges"` to choose bin counts
    automatically, matching NumPy (#42199).
  * Added the keyword-only `device` argument to `jax.numpy.logspace` and
    `jax.numpy.geomspace` (#41659).
  * Added the keyword-only `correction` argument (NumPy 2.0 alias for `ddof`)
    to `jax.numpy.nanvar` and `jax.numpy.nanstd`
    (#41696).
  * Added an optional `mode` keyword argument to `jax.random.normal`
    (controlled by the new `jax_random_normal_mode` config option, default
    `"low"`). `"low"` keeps existing behavior (truncating around ±5.3 standard
    deviations in `float32`); `"high"` uses more random bits per sample (~±6.3
    in `float32`, ±9.4 in `float64`), and `"highest"` uses two random streams
    to reach roughly ±9.1 in `float32` without enabling `x64`.
  * Added an optional keyword-only `mode` argument to
    `jax.random.truncated_normal` (default `"low"`). Setting `mode="high"`
    improves tail accuracy and eliminates boundary clamping spikes at extreme
    truncation bounds and in 16-bit floating-point types.
  * Added a keyword-only `num_streams` argument to `jax.random.bits` to
    generate a tuple of `1`, `2`, or `4` independent unsigned integer arrays in
    parallel from the underlying generator's native bit streams.
  * Added optional `out_sharding` support to `jax.lax.scatter` (and
    `scatter_add`, `scatter_sub`, `scatter_mul`, `scatter_min`, `scatter_max`,
    `scatter_apply`), `jax.lax.gather`, `jax.numpy.take`
    (`Array.take`), `jax.numpy.take_along_axis`, `jax.numpy.sum`,
    `jax.numpy.max`, `jax.numpy.quantile`,
    `jax.numpy.nanquantile`, and `jax.numpy.nanpercentile` (and
    native pass-through in `jax.numpy.percentile`).
  * `jax.lax.top_k`, `jax.lax.approx_max_k`, and
    `jax.lax.approx_min_k` now support sharded reduction axes under
    explicit sharding.
  * `jax.dlpack.from_dlpack` (and `jax.numpy.from_dlpack`) now
    accept `jax.experimental.layout.Format` in their `device` argument to
    specify device-local layouts (such as a linear layout `tiling=((1,),)` for
    TPU pinned host memory buffers, `kDLTPUHost`; `Layout.AUTO` is not
    supported). When `copy=None`, importing `kDLTPUHost` buffers now falls back
    to copying if zero-copy sharing is not possible.
  * `jax.experimental.serialize_executable.serialize` now supports saving
    and loading compiled functions that capture large constant arrays (see
    Breaking changes regarding format version).
  * [ROCm] Added `pip` extras (`jax[rocm]`, `jax[rocm7]`, `jax[rocm10]`, and
    per-GPU-target `jax[rocm7-device-<gfxNNN>]` /
    `jax[rocm10-device-<gfxNNN>]`) to install AMD's TheRock ROCm wheels directly
    from AMD's package index without a pre-installed system ROCm
    (`jax[rocm7-local]` remains for pre-installed ROCm) (#41331).

* Breaking changes
  * The `jax_use_simplified_jaxpr_constants` configuration flag is now `True`
    by default. Non-scalar constant arrays captured from outside a jitted
    function are now passed as separate inputs to compiled executables rather
    than embedded inline, reducing executable size and avoiding host copies
    during lowering. See the constants note in the JAX documentation for details, including how to
    recognize a breakage and migrate your code. You can temporarily set
    `JAX_USE_SIMPLIFIED_JAXPR_CONSTANTS=False` to restore the previous behavior;
    the flag will be removed in a future release.
  * Removed support for the legacy GSPMD partitioner
    (`jax_use_shardy_partitioner=False`). JAX now always uses the Shardy
    partitioner, which has been the default for about a year. Custom
    partitioning rules in `jax.experimental.custom_partitioning` that only
    implement legacy GSPMD callbacks (instead of `sharding_rule`) now raise
    `NotImplementedError`.
  * Updated the binary format written by
    `jax.experimental.serialize_executable.serialize` to version 3 to
    support captured constant arrays. Loading executables saved with JAX
    `0.12.0` or earlier via
    `jax.experimental.serialize_executable.deserialize_and_load` now
    raises `ValueError`.
  * `jax.random` samplers now propagate `out_sharding` directly per shard
    instead of falling back to automatic sharding or inserting hidden
    all-gathers. Requesting an `out_sharding` that shards non-key dimensions
    now requires a partitionable generator (`threefry2x32`, `rbg`, or
    `unsafe_rbg`, with `jax_threefry_partitionable=True`), raising
    `NotImplementedError` otherwise. Conflicting parameter shardings or
    sharding non-batch axes in composite samplers (`permutation`,
    `categorical`, `multivariate_normal`, `orthogonal`, `poisson`) now raise
    `ShardingTypeError`.
  * `jax.random.poisson` with `method="exact"` (the default) now keeps
    the first accepted sample per element so draws do not depend on how the
    array is sharded across devices. This can change the exact integer values
    drawn for multi-element arrays when `lam >= 10`.
  * `jax.numpy.histogram` now requires `out_sharding` to be fully
    replicated (raising `ShardingTypeError` otherwise) and, under explicit
    sharding, requires `weights` to match the sharding of `a`.
  * `jax.scipy.signal.welch` and `jax.scipy.signal.csd` (as well as
    `jax.scipy.signal.stft` when explicitly passed `nperseg=None`) now
    default `nperseg` to `256` when `window` is a string or tuple, matching
    SciPy and the documentation. Previously, inputs longer than `256` used the
    full signal length, so output shapes and values may change
    (#40012).

* Deprecations
  * `jax.sharding.SingleDeviceSharding` is deprecated. Use
    `jax.sharding.make_single_device_sharding` to construct a single-device
    sharding, and `jax.sharding.is_single_device_sharding` to check whether a
    sharding targets a single device (replacing
    `isinstance(..., SingleDeviceSharding)`).
  * The `jax_use_shardy_partitioner` configuration flag is deprecated and is now
    a no-op (setting it to `False` is silently ignored). JAX always uses the
    Shardy partitioner, and the flag will be removed in a future release.
  * `jax.scipy.special.bessel_jn` is deprecated; use
    `jax.scipy.special.jn` instead, which is more accurate and evaluates
    only the single `n`-th Bessel function directly (note that `bessel_jn`
    returned all orders `0..v`, whereas `jn(n, z)` returns only order `n`).

* Changes
  * On GPU, when neither `XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION` nor its deprecated alias
    `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION` is set, JAX now preallocates 75% of GPU
    memory at startup and allows the default GPU memory pool to grow up to
    available device memory as needed for ordinary (non-collective) buffers
    (XLA's `0.75+` policy). Set `XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.75` to keep the
    previous fixed limit. Explicit XLA memory-policy flags take precedence, and
    allocator modes that do not support growth retain their existing behavior
    (#41831).
  * Cached per-primitive compiled wrappers when running `jax.shard_map`
    eagerly (outside `jax.jit` or under `jax.disable_jit()`), avoiding repeated
    recompilation (#42470).
  * `jax.sharding.NamedSharding.shard_shape` now supports meshes with
    manual axes.
  * Enabled the custom derivative rule for `jax.nn.softmax` (and
    `jax.scipy.special.softmax`) by default
    (`jax_softmax_custom_jvp=True`), improving memory use and numerical
    stability during differentiation. Set
    `jax.config.update("jax_softmax_custom_jvp", False)` to temporarily restore
    the previous behavior.
  * On CPU, `jax.lax.log` and `jax.lax.log1p` now use vectorized
    kernels on x86-64 (AVX2/AVX-512) and ARM64 (NEON), speeding up `float64` by
    1.7×–4.4× and `float32` by 19%–37%. This improves `float32` accuracy for
    `log1p`, `log10`, `logit`, `acosh`, `asinh`, and `atanh`, and relaxes
    `float64` CPU `log` max error from 0.5 to 1.5 units in the last place
    (ULPs), matching GPU; CPU tests expecting bit-exact `float64` `log` may see
    ~1 ULP shifts.
  * On GPU and TPU, `accumulate` for `jax.numpy.bitwise_and`,
    `jax.numpy.bitwise_or`, `jax.numpy.bitwise_xor`,
    `jax.numpy.logical_and`, `jax.numpy.logical_or`,
    `jax.numpy.logical_xor`, `jax.numpy.maximum`, and
    `jax.numpy.minimum` now uses a parallel prefix scan for integer and
    boolean outputs, which is much faster for long axes (#28097).
  * `jax.scipy.fft.dct` and `jax.scipy.fft.idct`
    (`jax.scipy.fft.idctn`) now use real FFTs (`rfft` / `irfft`) instead
    of full complex FFTs, speeding up batched `idct` by up to 2.7× on GPU and
    9.4× on CPU (#42467, #42583).
  * Simplified gradients of `jax.numpy.logaddexp` and
    `jax.numpy.logaddexp2` using `jax.lax.logistic`, making
    gradient evaluation ~2–3× faster on CPU. Note that the gradient at
    `(inf, inf)` now returns `nan` instead of `1.0` (#41914).
  * Replaced large elementwise computations for `jax.lax.lgamma`
    (`jax.scipy.special.gammaln`) and `jax.lax.digamma`
    (`jax.scipy.special.digamma`) with dedicated vectorized CPU kernels
    (using `highway`, added as a `MODULE.bazel` dependency) and GPU kernels
    (CUDA/ROCm), improving compile time and speed while keeping error within
    0.5 ULP (`bfloat16`) and 1.0 ULP (`float16`, `float32`, `float64`) across
    CPU, GPU, and TPU. Also preserves very small (subnormal) inputs on GPU
    instead of returning `±inf`.
  * Mixed real and complex `jax.numpy.add`, `jax.numpy.subtract`,
    `jax.numpy.multiply`, and `jax.numpy.true_divide`
    (`complex / real`) no longer convert the real input to complex before
    operating. This avoids unnecessary operations on zeros and fixes edge cases
    with infinities and signed zeros (for example, `0.5 * (inf + 1j)` now
    returns `inf + 0.5j` instead of `inf + nan*j`).
  * Enabled a more accurate default implementation of `jax.lax.erfc` (and
    `jax.scipy.special.erfc`) (`jax_accurate_default_erfc=True`). It uses
    fewer operations, preserves very small (subnormal) outputs on CPU and GPU,
    returns `1.0` at `±0.0`, and reduces worst-case rounding error (`float32`:
    from ~66 down to ≤7.0 ULPs on CPU, ≤7.5 on GPU, ≤9.5 on TPU v6e/7x, and
    ≤69.0 on TPU v2–v5p; `float64`: from ≥350 down to ≤10.0 on CPU and GPU).
    With `accuracy=jax.lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`, worst-case error drops to
    ≤1.5–2.0 ULPs with fewer operations, and `bfloat16` drops from 63 to 25 ops
    with identical results. Set `jax_accurate_default_erfc=False` to temporarily
    restore the previous behavior.
  * Enabled the more accurate implementation of `jax.lax.erf_inv` by
    default (`jax_accurate_erf_inv=True`), fixing large precision loss near
    `|x| = 1` (`float32`: ~65 down to ≤2.0 ULPs on CPU, ≤2.5 on GPU/TPU v6e/7x,
    and ≤5.5 on TPU v5p; `float64`: ~500,000 down to ≤2.5 ULPs on CPU and GPU).
    Also improved first- and higher-order derivative accuracy near `|x| = 1`.
    Callers such as `jax.scipy.special.erfinv`,
    `jax.scipy.special.ndtri`, and default normal random samplers may see
    small last-bit numerical changes; set `jax_accurate_erf_inv=False` to
    temporarily restore the previous behavior.
  * `jax.lax.exp2` / `jax.numpy.exp2` and `jax.lax.log2` /
    `jax.numpy.log2` now lower directly to native operations and support
    `accuracy=jax.lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`, greatly reducing rounding error
    across dtypes and backends (for example, `exp2` `float32` CPU: 68.5 → 0.5
    ULP, GPU: 69.0 → 2.5 ULP; `float64` CPU: 719.0 → 0.5 ULP, GPU: 719.0 → 1.0
    ULP).
  * Improved numerical accuracy across several math and special functions:
    * `jax.scipy.special.gamma` and `jax.scipy.special.factorial`:
      ≤0.5 ULP (`bfloat16`) and ≤1.0 ULP (`float16`/`float32`/`float64`) across
      CPU, GPU, and TPU; exact `factorial` up to `34!` (`float32`) and `170!`
      (`float64`); preserves subnormal inputs on GPU.
    * `jax.lax.sinh` and `jax.lax.cosh`: vectorized CPU/TPU
      implementations cut `float32` error to ≤1.0 ULP (down from 25 ULPs on CPU
      and up to ~1794 ULPs on TPU) and `float64` CPU error from 496 to ≤2.0
      ULPs, and fix premature `sinh` overflow near `±89.4`.
    * `jax.lax.asin` and `jax.lax.acos`: improved CPU and TPU
      `float32` error to ≤1.0 ULP and stopped flushing tiny normal inputs to
      zero in `asin` on TPU.
    * `jax.lax.rsqrt`: tightened `float32` CPU error to ≤1.0 ULP on AVX
      x86-64 CPUs (≤1.5 ULP on ARM) by always running two refinement steps on
      both Intel and AMD CPUs.
    * `jax.lax.bessel_i0e` and `jax.lax.bessel_i1e`: faster
      implementation (~32 vs 85 ops in `float32`) cutting `float32` error from
      8.0 / 15.5 down to ≤2.0–3.0 ULPs and `float64` from 7.5–10.5 down to ≤2.0
      ULPs.
    * `jax.scipy.special.logit`: fixed severe precision loss near `0.5`
      and `1` (≤2.0–3.0 ULPs in `float32`, ≤1.5 ULPs in `float64` on CPU/GPU).
    * `jax.scipy.special.betaln` and `jax.scipy.stats.t.logpdf`:
      rewritten `betaln` improves accuracy for extreme ratios and negative or
      tiny inputs (raising `ValueError` for complex inputs), and `t.logpdf`
      avoids catastrophic cancellation for large degrees of freedom and in
      `float32` on TPU (#38243, #39106,
      #41203).
    * `jax.scipy.special.ndtr` and `jax.scipy.special.log_ndtr`:
      fixed large negative-tail error, positive-input precision loss, premature
      overflow, and derivative `NaN`s, with accurate higher-order derivatives
      (#41676).
    * `jax.lax.logistic` (`jax.nn.sigmoid`,
      `jax.scipy.special.expit`): avoids overflow for large negative
      inputs on GPU and in `float16` across all backends, preserving very small
      (subnormal) outputs instead of flushing prematurely to `0.0`.
  * JAX now uses Bazel 9.3.1 to build from source.
  * Linux and macOS source builds now compile with C++20 (Windows remains on
    C++17). Linux wheels are built with LLVM 22, statically linked `libc++`,
    and a `glibc 2.27` (`manylinux_2_27`) sysroot. Hermetic CUDA 13 builds
    upgraded from CUDA `13.0.0` to `13.4.1`, and CUDA 12 source builds now
    compile device code with Clang.
  * Bumped the pinned `libtpu` dependency for `jax[tpu]` from `0.0.50.*` to
    `0.0.53.*` (#42544).
  * Added support for building `jaxlib` against 64-bit integer BLAS/LAPACK
    libraries (`-DJAX_LAPACK_ILP64`), and fixed
    `jax.scipy.linalg.lu_solve` when SciPy uses 64-bit integer LAPACK
    with `jax_enable_x64=True`.
  * [oneAPI] Plugin wheels are now built with C++20 and target
    `manylinux_2_31` (`glibc 2.31`), allowing installation on older Linux
    distributions (#42568).

* Bug fixes
  * Fixed separate `jax.jit` instances of the same function that differ
    only in `static_argnums`, `static_argnames`, or `keep_unused` sharing
    internal dispatch cache entries, which could run the executable compiled
    for one instance with the arguments of another and return wrong results
    (#42313).
  * Added `jax_high_dynamic_range_gumbel` to the `jax.jit` cache key
    (#40609).
  * Fixed collective operations inside CPU loops (`jax.lax.while_loop`)
    and conditionals (`jax.lax.cond`) overlapping with later collectives,
    which could swap messages across processes or crash.
  * Fixed a thread-pool deadlock when multiple batched CPU linear algebra
    (LAPACK) calls run concurrently.
  * Fixed a crash (`SIGSEGV`) during complex GPU eigendecomposition
    (`jax.lax.linalg.eig` / `jax.numpy.linalg.eig`) when using
    MAGMA due to insufficient host buffer alignment.
  * Fixed a crash (`std::bad_function_call`) in `jaxlib` when transferring
    duplicate host shards with forced copying enabled (for example,
    `jax.device_put(..., may_alias=False)`).
  * Fixed a potential crash when registering multi-stage foreign function
    interface (FFI) targets via `jax.ffi.register_ffi_target` (where the
    `record` callback pointer was left uninitialized), and added support for
    the `"record"` handler stage.
  * Fixed CPU Python callbacks (`jax.pure_callback`,
    `jax.experimental.io_callback`, and
    `jax.experimental.buffer_callback`) flushing very small (subnormal)
    floating-point values to zero.
  * Fixed XLA compiler and runtime issues shipped in `jaxlib`:
    * Out-of-memory failures for large GPU allocations (> 1 GiB) on WSL
      despite sufficient free memory, by falling back to 1 GiB physical chunks
      mapped into one contiguous virtual address range
      (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52820).
    * Wrong numerical results on CPU when fusing a matrix multiplication with a
      broadcasted constant right-hand operand and a reduction
      (#41414, #42549).
    * Wrong numerical results on ARM64 SME/SME2 CPUs when fusing a matrix
      multiplication with a constant left-hand operand and a reduction
      (#42651).
    * Wrong results on Hopper/Blackwell NVIDIA GPUs (`sm_90+`, CUDA 13.4+) for
      large-stride `float64` column scatter overwrites (#41888).
    * Crash compiling a full-slice update (`.at[:].set(...)`) immediately
      followed by reversing the array (`[::-1]`) (#41497).
    * `lax.log(lax.pow(a, b))` returning finite values instead of `NaN` for
      negative bases under `jax.jit` (#41261).
    * Properly marks donated CPU buffers as deleted when an active host view
      forces a copy, and marks multi-device arrays as deleted when donating a
      non-first shard (#41256).
  * Fixed `jax.lax.pmean` and constant `jax.lax.psum` dividing or
    multiplying every group by the first group's size when `axis_index_groups`
    has uneven group sizes (#41132).
  * Fixed batching, autodiff, and sharding bugs in
    `jax.lax.ragged_all_to_all` (#41697).
  * Fixed `jax.lax.while_loop` seeing stale values or dropping final
    writes when `cond_fun` reads or writes a mutable `Ref`
    (#41073).
  * Fixed `jax.lax.polynomial` errors inside `jax.shard_map` with
    mixed constant and varying inputs (#41853).
  * Prevented silent wrong results (counting constants once per device) when
    mixing unreduced or reduced arrays (under explicit sharding or `shard_map`)
    with replicated constants in `pad`, `concatenate`/`stack`, and `select_n`.
  * Fixed `out_sharding` being silently ignored when array indexing lowers to
    static or dynamic slicing.
  * Fixed `full_like` / `empty_like` in partially manual `jax.shard_map`,
    mesh context mismatches when differentiating `jax.jit` with `explicit_axes`,
    and false-positive `ForbiddenCollectiveError` in
    `jax.sharding.no_collectives` on 3-operand `einsum`.
  * Fixed `jax.ref.new_ref(..., pin=True)` errors when reading/writing pinned
    references (#41846) or pinning buffers to TPU VMEM
    (#41843).
  * Fixed sharded `philox2x32` / `philox4x32` (`lax.mulhi`) forward-compatibility
    export and compatibility with older `jaxlib` builds.
  * Fixed `jax.export` dropping `weak_type` on outputs across `serialize` and
    `deserialize` (bumping serialization format from 12 to 13,
    backward-compatible with older payloads) (#41007), baking
    caller stack traces into exported MLIR modules (causing non-deterministic
    exports and cache misses), and lowering `jax.lax.platform_dependent`
    branches for incompatible platforms during multi-platform export.
  * Fixed gradient `Ref` accumulator forwarding in
    `jax.custom_vjp.defvjp_with_accums` and
    `jax.custom_gradient(with_accums=...)` through `checkpoint`, `jit`, `scan`,
    and `checkify`; also fixed `remat` with tuple `prevent_cse` and closed-over
    constants, improved leaked-tracer error messages, and avoided copying in
    `jax.numpy.moveaxis` when no axes move (#41717).
  * Fixed `jax.vmap` of `jax.numpy.stack` emitting an unnecessary
    transpose when stacking along the batched axis (#41794).
  * Fixed out-of-bounds unsigned integer indices (such as large `uint64` or
    `uint32` values) wrapping around modulo `2**32` instead of clamping when
    cast to signed `int32` during indexing (#42657).
  * Fixed overflow when wrapping negative indices of narrow signed integer
    dtypes (such as `int8(-1)`) on long axes across indexing, dynamic slicing,
    `jax.numpy.take`, and `jax.numpy.put`; also made `jax.ds`
    slices consistent between eager and `jit` execution (#42354,
    #42377).
  * Fixed `jax.numpy.interp` returning `nan` at and around sample points
    whose `fp` value is infinite; it now returns the sample value or the signed
    infinity, matching NumPy. For complex `fp`, the real and imaginary parts
    are now interpolated separately, as in NumPy (#42318). Also
    fixed `interp` mishandling narrow intervals, duplicate trailing `xp`
    coordinates, `NaN` query inputs, and `NaN` derivatives at narrow or
    duplicate boundaries (#42650).
  * Fixed `jax.numpy.modf` returning `nan` as the fractional part for
    infinite inputs; it now returns a signed zero, matching NumPy
    (#41102).
  * Fixed `jax.numpy.nonzero`, `jax.numpy.flatnonzero`, and
    `jax.numpy.argwhere` ignoring `fill_value` on empty arrays
    (#42233).
  * Fixed `jax.numpy.nan_to_num` overwriting custom replacement values a
    second time when replacing `NaN` with infinity (#42406).
  * Fixed infinite loops in `jax.numpy.gcd` and `jax.numpy.lcm` for
    minimum representable signed integers such as `int32(-2**31)`
    (#40840).
  * Fixed `jax.numpy.choose` wrapping indices when the number of choices
    exceeds a narrow index dtype's maximum (#42464).
  * Fixed `jax.numpy.kron` and `jax.numpy.vander` failing on
    boolean inputs (#42462).
  * Fixed weighted `jax.numpy.quantile`, `jax.numpy.nanquantile`,
    `jax.numpy.percentile`, and `jax.numpy.nanpercentile` (with
    `method="inverted_cdf"`) returning zero-weight elements at `q=0`
    (#42190).
  * `jax.scipy.linalg.polar` with `method="qdwh"` now honors
    `max_iterations` and accepts `eps`, as documented; previously
    `max_iterations` was silently ignored and any non-`None` `eps` raised a
    `ValueError`. Both `eps` and `max_iterations` are now static arguments of
    `polar` (for all `method` values), so passing a traced value for either
    raises an error (#41917).
  * Fixed wrong forward-mode derivatives (`jvp`) of pivoted QR decomposition
    (`jax.lax.linalg.qr`, `jax.scipy.linalg.qr`) for wide matrices
    (`m < n`) (#42634).
  * Fixed `jax.scipy.linalg.toeplitz` and `jax.scipy.linalg.hankel`
    spreading a single `NaN` or `inf` across the entire output matrix
    (#38635, #38636).
  * Fixed `jax.scipy.sparse.linalg.cg` producing `NaN`s or stopping early
    when the right-hand side or initial guess has very small or very large
    magnitude (for example, during differentiation with a preconditioner)
    (#40254).
  * Fixed `jax.scipy.signal.convolve`, `convolve2d`, `correlate`, and
    `correlate2d` raising `ValueError` on mixed-size multidimensional arrays
    for `mode="full"` and `mode="same"`, matching SciPy (#42063).
  * Fixed wrong derivatives for padded entries in
    `jax.experimental.sparse.coo_fromdense` and
    `jax.experimental.sparse.csr_fromdense` (`COO`/`CSR`/`CSC.fromdense`)
    when `nse > nnz` (#40624).
  * Fixed `jax.experimental.sparse.bcoo_reshape` (`BCOO.reshape`)
    miscomputing shapes for sparse arrays with dense dimensions
    (#24795).
  * Fixed overflow and underflow in derivatives of division (`x / y`,
    `jax.lax.div`) for very large or very small denominators
    (#37909).
  * Fixed overflow, cancellation in higher-order derivatives, and `NaN`
    gradients at single-axis infinities for complex `jax.numpy.abs`,
    `jax.numpy.hypot`, and `jax.numpy.arctan2`
    (`jax.lax.atan2`) (#25681).
  * Fixed `jax.nn.soft_sign` returning `NaN` at `±inf` (now returns `±1`)
    and losing derivative accuracy for large inputs.
  * Fixed `jax.nn.softmax` with `where` leaking `NaN` into gradients when
    masked-out positions have `NaN` or infinite tangents/cotangents.
  * Fixed overflow and out-of-domain derivatives in `jax.nn.log1mexp`.
  * Fixed overflow and precision loss in `jax.nn.squareplus` for large
    inputs in `float16` (#41647).
  * Fixed a shape/broadcasting error in
    `jax.nn.get_scaled_dot_general_config` for `'nvfp4'`
    (#42025).
  * Fixed wrong higher-order derivatives of `jax.scipy.special.fresnel`
    at odd integers and `0`.
  * Fixed premature overflow in `jax.scipy.special.i0`
    (`jax.numpy.i0`) and `jax.scipy.special.i1` for large finite
    inputs (#39770, #39772).
  * Fixed `jax.scipy.special.expi` returning `NaN` instead of `inf` at
    `+inf` (#38519).
  * Fixed `jax.scipy.special.loggamma` returning `NaN` instead of `inf` at
    `0.0` and `-0.0` (#38240).
  * Fixed `jax.scipy.special.zeta` and
    `jax.scipy.special.polygamma` for large or infinite `q`
    (#41366).
  * Fixed `NaN` gradients in `jax.scipy.stats.pareto` methods outside the
    distribution's domain (#41445).
  * Fixed `float32` precision loss in `jax.scipy.stats.nbinom.logpmf`
    (#42145).
  * Fixed `logpmf` and `pmf` for discrete distributions in `jax.scipy.stats`
    (`betabinom`, `bernoulli`, `binom`, `geom`, and `nbinom`) to return `-inf`
    (`0` for `pmf`) for non-integer `k - loc`, matching SciPy; also fixed `loc`
    bound checks in `betabinom` (#41745, #41960).
  * Fixed `jax.random.poisson` returning undefined values or raising
    under `jax.debug_nans(True)` when `lam` is infinite or non-finite
    (#38335).
  * Fixed `jax.random.multivariate_normal` with `method="eigh"` returning
    `NaN` on singular or near-singular covariance matrices (#14345).
  * Fixed `jax.random.choice` dropping other array dimensions when
    drawing zero samples (#42429).
  * Fixed `jax.debug.breakpoint` with `backend="web"` crashing under
    `web-pdb` 2.x.
  * Preserved operation name (`op_name`) metadata in compiled HLO when
    `jax_include_full_tracebacks_in_locations=False` (#41587).
  * Fixed crashes in `jax_explain_cache_misses=True` when `debug_info` is
    passed as a keyword argument (#41455) or argument names are
    unknown.

json.description: For developers, who are building real-time data-driven applications, Redis is the preferred, fastest, and most feature-rich cache, data structure server, and document and vector query engine.

json.body:
This is the General Availability release of Redis 8.12 in Redis Open Source.

### Major changes compared to 8.10

- Compressed bitmaps — Integrated redis-roaring into Redis core for lower memory usage and faster bitmap operations. 
Special thanks to Antonio Viggiano, the original creator of redis-roaring, for contributing this capability!
- Substantial memory reduction for large sorted set with a new B+ tree encoding 
- New command: `BITRANGEINTARRAY` equivalent to redis-roaring’s `R.RANGEINTARRAY`, to return set bit offsets within a specified range
- Set member expiration: New commands: `SEXPIRE`,`SPEXPIRE`,`SEXPIREAT`,`SPEXPIREAT` - set expiration of a Set member; `STTL`, `SPTTL`, `SEXPIRETIME`,`SPEXPIRETIME` - retrieve remaining TTLs or expiration timestamps; `SETPERSIST` - remove the expiration of members 
- New command: `BLESS` - avoid eviction of specified keys
- New commands: `ZMOVE`, `BZMOVE` and ‘ZMOVEMEMBER‘ - atomic sorted-set moves for end-of-set batches and destination conditions 
- Count-min-sketch extensions
- Auto create JSON deep path
- Opt-in SQ8 new compression is now available for HNSW vector indexes
- `CLUSTER MIGRATION STATUS` now reports progress for both the snapshot and incremental migration phases
- Redis query engine: `FT.ALTER` avoids unnecessary document reindexing during schema additions
- Redis query engine: `EXPLAINSCORE` is now supported for `FT.HYBRID`
- Redis query engine: `RETURN_STRICT` timeout handling is now enabled for local `FT.HYBRID` execution

### Bug fixes (compared to 8.12 RC-3)

- #16252 HOTKEYS GET reported a wrong collection-duration-ms after 2^31 milliseconds
- #16219 HPERSIST ignored a replicated or AOF persist of a field the local clock had already expired
- #16207 Replicas misbehaved when replication compression was enabled
- #16267 BITCOUNT returned wrong results on AArch64 for large dense bitmaps 
- #16081 Addresses and names announced on the cluster bus were accepted without validation 
- RedisTimeSeries/RedisTimeSeries#2234 Fix a crash when loading persisted compaction rules with an invalid aggregation type (MOD-20881).
- RedisJSON/RedisJSON#1692 Fix JSON.ARRINSERT partially modifying arrays before returning a validation error (MOD-9116).
- RedisBloom/RedisBloom#1090 Improve TopK write performance by initializing the seed generator once, reducing per-command random-seed generation overhead.

json.name: valkey
json.description: A flexible distributed key-value database that is optimized for caching and other realtime workloads.

json.body:
Valkey 9.2.1  -  Released Wed 25 November 2026
----------------------------------------------

Upgrade urgency MODERATE: Program an upgrade of the server, but it's not urgent.

### Bug Fixes
* Restore pre-9.2 TLS loading so the server no longer refuses to start or apply TLS configuration when a loaded certificate, such as an expired root left in a `tls-ca-cert-file` bundle, is outside its validity period by @madolson (#5550)
* Fix a server crash when `PHGET` reads a large path hash while a forkless save is running by @madolson (#5112)
* Fix a double mutex unlock, which is undefined behavior, when reducing the number of IO threads at runtime by @sarthakaggarwal97 (#5366)
* Fix dual-channel replication so a replica aborts and resyncs when the primary link breaks while it applies its local buffer, instead of reporting a successful sync on a dead link by @shohamazon (#5417)
* Fix IO threads resending already-written data to a client that is being closed, which could make a replica dropped for exceeding `client-output-buffer-limit` fail with a protocol error by @dgershko (#5468)
* Fix `COMMAND GETKEYS EXEC` returning wrong keys and possibly crashing the server when given more than 256 conditions by @madolson (#4712)
* Fix an uninitialized memory read in `ValkeyModule_CloseKey` when a module changes the type of an open key through `ValkeyModule_Call` by @Baraa-Hasheesh (#5358)
* Fix a use-after-free that could crash a cluster node receiving a cluster bus forgotten-node extension in which the sender names itself by @roshkhatri (#4675)
* Fix cluster nodes adopting stale replica claims that form a replication cycle in their cluster view, which could trigger an assertion crash in builds with debug assertions by @Baraa-Hasheesh (#5452)
* Fix a possible assertion crash with IO threads when more data arrives for a client that has a partially received command and is pending close by @aradz44 (#3245)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey/compare/9.2.0...9.2.1

json.body:
- [CHANGE] API: The experimental search endpoints now clamp `batch_size` to 1000. #19731
- [CHANGE] Configuration: Default --web.external-url to https when --web.config.file enables TLS. #19241
- [CHANGE] PromQL: Subquery samples are now included in the query TotalSamples and TotalSamplesPerStep statistics, and SamplesRead now counts reads from subqueries with an @ modifier in range queries. #19165
- [CHANGE] Remote write: Stop exposing the deprecated `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_total`, `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_failed_total`, `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_retried_total`, and `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_bytes_total` metrics for Remote Write 2.0 queues. #20080
- [CHANGE] Remote write receiver: Count Remote Write 2.x samples and histograms ingested without metadata in `prometheus_api_remote_write_without_metadata_appended_samples_total` even when `metadata-wal-records` is disabled. #19812
- [CHANGE] TSDB: Reject exemplars whose label names are not unique, instead of storing them and serving a duplicate JSON key from `/api/v1/query_exemplars`. #19896
- [FEATURE] API: Allow overriding PromQL Start Timestamp processing on a per-query basis using the `X-Prometheus-Use-Start-Timestamps` HTTP header. #19066
- [FEATURE] Agent: Support metadata-wal-records in Prometheus Agent mode. #19684
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Add experimental `integral()` function for computing integral-over-time of range vectors behind the `--enable-feature=promql-experimental-functions` flag. #14440
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Add experimental query cost estimation, actual cost reporting, and configurable execution limits, enabled with `--enable-feature=query-cost`. #20028
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Smoothed and Anchored vector selectors are now stable and always-on. #19697
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Use start timestamps to detect counter resets when float timeseries are queried using extended range selector modifiers (`anchored`, `smoothed`). This feature is hidden behind `use-start-timestamps` feature flag. #18966
- [FEATURE] Promtool: print test filename during promtool tests #18271
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Allow unquoted Unicode letters and dots behind a feature flag #20162
- [ENHANCEMENT] Search API: Warn when participating remote-read storage does not support search. #19992
- [ENHANCEMENT] Remote Read: Add native histogram prometheus_remote_read_handler_gate_wait_duration_seconds to measure concurrency-gate wait duration, including requests canceled while waiting. #18355
- [ENHANCEMENT] Remote Write: Add experimental flag `convert_nhcb_to_classic` to convert NHCB to classic histograms for external systems that dont support NHCBs. #17205
- [ENHANCEMENT] promtool: Add `--allow-incompatible-block-duration` so users can specify any max-block-duration instead of being restricted to the default Prometheus block durations. #19363
- [PERF] Remote write: Cache repeated OTLP histogram metric names. #19717
- [PERF] OpenMetrics 2.0 parser: Reuse classic histogram and summary expansion buffers across scrapes. #19907
- [PERF] PromQL: Decode only histogram sum/count (not buckets) for timestamp(), start_timestamp() and absent(). #19738
- [PERF] PromQL: Only select the fixed window for subqueries with an `@` modifier. #19863
- [PERF] Remote write / TSDB: Deduplicate per-series metadata structs in memory with `unique.Handle`. #20040
- [PERF] Scrape: Avoid some copies of scrape response bodies. #19394
- [PERF] TSDB: Improve XOR2 compression and append performance by selecting value windows based on encoding cost. #19962
- [PERF] TSDB: Reduce memory used writing and reading checkpoint metadata records. #19712
- [PERF] Scrape: Convert classic histograms to NHCB directly in the OpenMetrics 2.0 parser without wrapping in `NHCBParser`. #19880
- [PERF] Scrape: Reduce OpenMetrics 2.0 parser allocations and CPU overhead by lazily constructing composite series and exemplar labels. #19895
- [BUGFIX] Remote read: Abort failed streaming responses without writing duplicate headers or appending plain-text errors to the protobuf stream #19749
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix loss of out-of-order samples when a WAL checkpoint drops a series record that the out-of-order write-behind log still needs #19737
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix queries that seek within a head chunk returning samples committed after the query started #19854
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Preserve mapped chunks when WAL replay merges multiple references for the same series, preventing missing out-of-order samples and duplicate in-order chunks after restart #19805
- [BUGFIX] Fix auto-reload logic to reload after reverting a failed configuration change #19838
- [BUGFIX] API: Do not match metric family metadata for doubled _total and _info suffixes in experimental search API. #19910
- [BUGFIX] API: Reject `timeout` and `lookback_delta` values that overflow int64 instead of turning them into a negative duration #19658
- [BUGFIX] API: Resolve metric family metadata for suffixed metric names in search results, in experimental search API. #19824
- [BUGFIX] AWS SD: Describe each ElastiCache cluster once instead of twice for clusters that are not replication group members. #19434
- [BUGFIX] Build: Allow installing promtool with version-suffixed go install commands #19754
- [BUGFIX] Discovery: Fix a panic in Azure service discovery when a VM tag has a null value. #19755
- [BUGFIX] Federation: fix corruption of float native histograms. #19679
- [BUGFIX] Fix ts_of_last_over_time for samples before the Unix epoch. #19828
- [BUGFIX] Histograms: Fix ConvertNHCBToClassic inflating classic bucket counts for integer native histograms whose spans have gaps. #19659
- [BUGFIX] Logging: Preserve rule and TSDB block values in JSON logs. #19572
- [BUGFIX] OTLP receiver: Drop exemplars with timestamps more than 10 minutes in the future instead of storing them and blocking subsequent exemplars for that series. #19812
- [BUGFIX] OTLP: Count only out-of-order exemplars in `prometheus_api_otlp_out_of_order_exemplars_total`, not every rejected exemplar. #20030
- [BUGFIX] OTLP: Do not drop exemplars that have a `trace_id` or `span_id` filtered attribute in addition to a trace or span ID. The trace context now takes precedence over the colliding attribute, as required by the OpenTelemetry specification. #20004
- [BUGFIX] OTLP: Do not emit `le="+Inf"` twice when a histogram's explicit bounds end at `+Inf`, and warn about the bound. #19425
- [BUGFIX] OTLP: Stop dropping exemplars that arrive out of timestamp order within a data point. #20029
- [BUGFIX] OpenMetrics 2.0: Attach histogram exemplars to matching classic `_bucket` series and preserve them when scraping both native and classic histograms. #20020
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Avoid intermediate overflow in `rad()` and `deg()` conversions. #19901
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Consistently ignore and drop `__type__` and `__unit__` labels in `without` aggregations, `absent()`, `info()`, and binary operator fill matching. #19986
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Do not panic when printing the partial AST returned alongside a parse error. #19797
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Drop __type__ and __unit__ in binary operations so they are transparent to users, similar to how __name__ is handled. #18680
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix `==`, `!=`, `changes()` and `count_values` on native histograms giving wrong results inside `histogram_count()`, `histogram_sum()` and `histogram_avg()`. #20024
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix histogram_fraction returning wrong results for native histograms with custom buckets when a bucket boundary is exactly 0. #19657
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix histogram_quantile and histogram_quantiles interpolating within the wrong bucket for native histograms whose sum is NaN. #19973
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix lexing of subqueries whose range is a duration keyword expression, e.g. `foo[range():1s]`. #19729
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix warning and error locations for duration expressions `min_of` and `max_of`. #19742
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Ignore NaN classic histogram bucket boundaries in `histogram_quantile`, `histogram_quantiles` and `histogram_fraction` and return correct value instead of NaN if there are normal buckets. #20057
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Preserve infinite values at exact quantile ranks. #19899
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Preserve original operand sides for experimental fill modifiers with group_right matching. #19939
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Preserve subquery step expressions when printing queries after preprocessing. #19743
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: Range vector functions no longer raise a spurious "vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset" error when series have different metric names but the same remaining labels, as long as their timestamps do not overlap within the evaluated range window #18631
- [BUGFIX] PromQL: do not count subquery materialized samples in total samples statistics #19873
- [BUGFIX] Remote write: Prevent future-dated exemplars from scaling shards down to the minimum. #19866
- [BUGFIX] Agent: Prevent future sent timestamps from advancing WAL truncation beyond the minimum retention window. #19866
- [BUGFIX] Rules: Restore firing alerts with for durations shorter than --rules.alert.for-grace-period after a restart. #19882
- [BUGFIX] Scrape: fix failing scrape when float histogram is emitted over protobuf with count, zero count and buckets all zero, for example a result of recording `rate(x[1m])` over constant histogram. #19682
- [BUGFIX] Search API: Return the lexically smallest label values when `limit` is set on `/api/v1/search/label_values`, instead of an arbitrary subset #19694
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix WAL watcher permanently skipping checkpoint series garbage collection when lagging behind head truncation. #20041
- [BUGFIX] Search API: Avoid panics when the requested time range has no participating storage. #19992
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix a race in selected-series and stale-series compaction where a sample committed after the block was written but before the series was evicted from the head could be silently lost. The fix no longer depends on isolation being enabled. #19666
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix a rare case where a sample could be lost during selected-series or stale-series compaction if an unrelated write to the same series ran cleanup that erased the evidence needed to protect it. #19672
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Fix spurious "unknown series references" warnings during WAL replay after a restart, when the only blocks on disk were produced by selected-series or stale-series compaction. #19734
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Increment `prometheus_tsdb_wal_corruptions_total` when WAL corruption is detected during checkpoint creation, so the metric reflects corruption found at compaction time rather than only after a restart-triggered repair. #19858
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Preserve series identities needed to recover exemplars after compaction and restart. #19940
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: Reject native histograms whose span offsets overflow the int32 bucket index instead of storing them with corrupted buckets. #20034
- [BUGFIX] TSDB: fix no passing metadata-wal-records to TSDB from main feature flag. #19678
- [BUGFIX] Templates: Preserve IPv6 addresses with dotted zone identifiers in `stripDomain`. #19908
- [BUGFIX] UI: Don't automatically open an autocomplete dropdown after closing a function call body or aggregation operator with a closing parenthesis. #19825
- [BUGFIX] Web: Fix HTTP/2 negotiation silently falling back to HTTP/1.1 under Go 1.27+ when TLS is enabled with `http2: true`. The server now correctly advertises `h2` via ALPN and multiplexes concurrent requests over a single connection. #19848
- [BUGFIX] mixin: Fix double-counting of failed samples in the `PrometheusRemoteStorageFailures` alert denominator. #19877
- [BUGFIX] promtool: Honor `--enable-feature` when evaluating rules in `test rules`. #20046
- [BUGFIX] Scrape: Ensure UTF-8 works with the experimental OpenMetrics 2.0 #19902
- [BUGFIX] Scrape: Reject sum-only classic histograms during NHCB conversion #19315

### 2.9.8 / 2026.10.21

- fix(compile): check read permission for dynamically imported local files
  (#36925)
- fix(completions): complete script paths for bare deno run in zsh (#36976)
- fix(core): keep op contexts alive until the isolate is disposed (#37026)
- fix(coverage): skip the V8 code cache while collecting coverage (#36901)
- fix(ext/fetch): bump hyper-util to 0.1.21 and hyper to 1.11.1 to cancel idle
  interval when pool empties (#36968)
- fix(ext/napi): check napi_create_dataview bounds for overflow (#36962)
- fix(ext/napi): ignore the callback return value while an exception is pending
  (#36942)
- fix(ext/node): align X.509v1 certificate handling with OpenSSL (#36933)
- fix(ext/node): mock.reset() restores mock.method() implementations (#36886)
- fix(ext/node): support assert message functions and format arguments (#36944)
- fix(npm): validate package link names (#37047)
- fix(tls): distrust compromised eMudhra certificate authorities (#37046)
- fix: bump rand 0.9.x to patched version

json.name: Bun v1.4.5
json.body:
To install Bun v1.4.5
```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash
# or you can use npm
# npm install -g bun
```

Windows:
```bash
powershell -c "irm bun.com/install.ps1|iex"
```

To upgrade to Bun v1.4.5:
```bash
bun upgrade
```

### [Read Bun v1.4.5's release notes on Bun's blog](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.5)

### Thanks to 3 contributors!

- [@dylan-conway](https://github.com/dylan-conway)
- [@Jarred-Sumner](https://github.com/Jarred-Sumner)
- [@robobun](https://github.com/robobun)

### Breaking Changes 🛠

- (apidocs) Declare the API base path in the spec's server URL by @BYK with @sentry-junior in [#131065](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/131065)
- (typing) Enforce strict mypy across Sentry's Python codebase (types only) by @joshuarli with @sentry-junior in [#129614](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129614)

### New Features ✨

#### Aci

- Allow equations in span metric monitors behind a flag by @mrduncan with @sentry-junior in [#130742](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130742)
- Only query "alert" Worfklow.type on frontend by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129272](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129272)
- Update workflow engine documentation for Workflow.type by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129271](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129271)
- Handle Workflow type in secondary callers by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129270](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129270)
- Handle hidden workflows in detector endpoints by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129269](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129269)
- Handle Workflow type field on API endpoints by @RudraPatel2003 with @getsantry in [#129268](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129268)
- Add type/organization index to Workflow table by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129267](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129267)
- Add type field to Workflow model by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129266](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129266)
- Fix DataError in uptime check-ins by @RudraPatel2003 in [#129974](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129974)

#### Admin

- Add Enable Restricted Members customer action by @volokluev with @sentry-junior in [#130936](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130936)
- Allow removing a sponsorship from a customer by @noahsmartin in [#130801](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130801)
- Add a Simulate LLM usage action to customer details by @volokluev with @sentry-junior in [#130323](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130323)
- Add a modal to grant ledger credit by @volokluev and @claude in [#129809](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129809)
- Add action to set a customer's contract package by @noahsmartin in [#128965](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/128965)

#### Agent Handoff

- Serve the handoff guide at /agent-handoff.md by @Abdkhan14 with @sentry-junior in [#131079](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/131079)
- Record prompt creation and claim analytics by @evanpurkhiser with @sentry-junior in [#131085](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/131085)

- Return handoff code from prompt endpoint by @evanpurkhiser with @sentry-junior in [#130909](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130909)
- Use create project flow in project setup by @evanpurkhiser in [#130843](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130843)
- Add create project flow by @evanpurkhiser in [#130835](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130835)
- Add reusable setup prompt by @evanpurkhiser in [#130747](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130747)
- Add prompt copy interactions by @evanpurkhiser in [#130693](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130693)
- Copy private prompts on demand by @evanpurkhiser in [#130675](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130675)

- Add Windows setup instructions by @evanpurkhiser in [#130110](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130110)
- Supply the secret token alongside the URL by @evanpurkhiser in [#130187](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130187)
- Select handoff flows at mint time by @evanpurkhiser in [#130089](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130089)

#### Agentic Onboarding

#### Api

- Move the @sentry/api package into static/packages/api by @BYK with @sentry-junior and @getsantry in [#130472](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130472)

- Add optional endpoint duration budgets by @kcons in [#129107](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129107)
- Type metric issue occurrence evidenceData in the API schema by @BYK with @sentry-junior in [#129585](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129585)
- Add opt-in max-age mode to ConditionalGetResponseMixin by @BYK with @sentry-junior in [#128828](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/128828)
- Let endpoints and code require a user by @gricha in [#129143](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/129143)

#### Apidocs

- Follow same-file helpers in S025-S028 by @akhilp117 in [#130267](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130267)
- Add S034 lint for undocumented inline 4xx responses by @BYK with @sentry-junior in [#131072](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/131072)
- Publish user details GET with token access by @sentry-junior in [#130368](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/130368)

Welcome to the v2.4.2 release of containerd! The second patch release for containerd 2.4 contains various fixes and updates including security patches. ### Security Updates * **containerd** * [**CVE-2026-95839**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-vwhp-8p66-mq4f) * [**GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc) * [**GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66) ### Highlights #### Container Runtime Interface (CRI) * Apply hardening to not follow symlinks for container log files ([#14302](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14302)) #### Image Distribution * Fix excessive memory usage during image pulls when registry downloads outpace content writes ([#14342](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14342)) * Apply hardening to reject image references with ".." path components ([#14282](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14282)) #### Runtime * Apply hardening to allowlist socket domains in the default seccomp profile ([#14247](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14247)) Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues. ### Contributors * Samuel Karp * Maksym Pavlenko * Sebastiaan van Stijn * Derek McGowan * LEI WANG * Paweł Gronowski * Phil Estes * Wei Fu * syed abdul khaliq ### Changes

### Dependency Changes This release has no dependency changes Previous release can be found at [v2.4.1](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.1) ### Which file should I download? * `containerd---.tar.gz`: ✅Recommended. Dynamically linked with glibc 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04). * `containerd-static---.tar.gz`: Statically linked. Expected to be used on Linux distributions that do not use glibc >= 2.35. Not position-independent. In addition to containerd, typically you will have to install [runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases) and [CNI plugins](https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins/releases) from their official sites too. See also the [Getting Started](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md) documentation.
